modules.title: Angular-momentum observables under a central force
modules.doc:
Squared angular momentum, its axial component, and their Poisson brackets for central forces.

## i. Overview

The angular momentum of a particle at position `q` with momentum `p` is `L = q × p`. This file
defines it on phase space, together with the two functions of it which Poisson-commute: its squared
magnitude `L² = ‖L‖²` and its component `L_z` along the z-axis. Their gradients follow from
Lagrange's identity `‖q × p‖² = ⟪q, q⟫ ⟪p, p⟫ - ⟪q, p⟫²` and the explicit form
`L_z = q₀ p₁ - q₁ p₀`.

We show that `L²` and `L_z` are in involution, and that both Poisson-commute with any Hamiltonian
whose momentum gradient is parallel to the momentum and whose position gradient is parallel to the
position. By `CentralForce.hasGradientAt_hamiltonian_momentum` and
`CentralForce.hasGradientAt_hamiltonian_position`, this includes the Hamiltonian of every
central-force system away from the centre of force, so `L²` and `L_z` are conserved by the motion.

## ii. Key results

- `CentralForce.angularMomentum` : the angular momentum `L = q × p`.
- `CentralForce.angularMomentumSq`, `CentralForce.angularMomentumZ` : `L²` and `L_z`.
- `CentralForce.angularMomentumSq_eq` : Lagrange's identity for `L²`.
- `CentralForce.poissonBracket_angularMomentumSq_angularMomentumZ` : `{L², L_z} = 0`.
- `CentralForce.poissonBracket_angularMomentumSq_hamiltonian`,
  `CentralForce.poissonBracket_angularMomentumZ_hamiltonian` : `L²` and `L_z` Poisson-commute with
  the Hamiltonian of a central-force system.
- `CentralForce.hamiltonian_angularMomentumZ_eq_on_Icc` gives conservation along an orbit.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The angular momentum
  - A.1. The squared magnitude and the z-component
  - A.2. Smoothness
- B. Gradients
- C. Poisson brackets
  - C.1. The squared magnitude and the z-component are in involution
  - C.2. Poisson brackets for radial partial gradients
  - C.3. Conservation under a central force
- D. Conservation along a trajectory

## iv. References

* H. Goldstein, C. Poole and J. Safko, *Classical Mechanics*, 3rd edition,
  Section 9.7 (Poisson bracket relations for angular momentum) and Chapter 3 (central forces).

At a phase-space point where the momentum gradient of a Hamiltonian is parallel to the momentum

vanish. These sufficient conditions apply to the central-force Hamiltonian away from the centre.

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.angularMomentum
declarations.doc: The angular momentum `L = q × p` of a particle at position `q` with momentum `p`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def angularMomentum (p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.angularMomentum_apply_zero
declarations.doc: The x-component of the angular momentum is `q₁ p₂ - q₂ p₁`.
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentum_apply_zero (p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :
    angularMomentum p q 0 = q 1 * p 2 - q 2 * p 1

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.angularMomentum_apply_one
declarations.doc: The y-component of the angular momentum is `q₂ p₀ - q₀ p₂`.
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentum_apply_one (p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :
    angularMomentum p q 1 = q 2 * p 0 - q 0 * p 2

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.angularMomentum_apply_two
declarations.doc: The z-component of the angular momentum is `q₀ p₁ - q₁ p₀`.
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentum_apply_two (p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :
    angularMomentum p q 2 = q 0 * p 1 - q 1 * p 0

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.angularMomentumSq
declarations.doc:
The squared magnitude `L² = ‖q × p‖²` of the angular momentum, as a function on phase
space.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def angularMomentumSq (p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) : ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.angularMomentumZ
declarations.doc: The component `L_z` of the angular momentum along the z-axis, as a function on phase space.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def angularMomentumZ (p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) : ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.angularMomentumSq_eq_sum
declarations.doc: The squared magnitude of the angular momentum is the sum of the squares of its components.
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentumSq_eq_sum (p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :
    angularMomentumSq p q =
      angularMomentum p q 0 ^ 2 + angularMomentum p q 1 ^ 2 + angularMomentum p q 2 ^ 2

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.angularMomentumSq_eq
declarations.doc:
Lagrange's identity: the squared magnitude of the angular momentum `q × p` is
`⟪q, q⟫ ⟪p, p⟫ - ⟪q, p⟫²`.
declarations.statement:
lemma angularMomentumSq_eq (p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :
    angularMomentumSq p q = ⟪q, q⟫_ℝ * ⟪p, p⟫_ℝ - ⟪q, p⟫_ℝ ^ 2

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.contDiff_angularMomentumSq
declarations.doc: The squared magnitude of the angular momentum is a smooth function on phase space.
declarations.statement: lemma contDiff_angularMomentumSq : ContDiff ℝ ∞ (Function.uncurry angularMomentumSq)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.contDiff_angularMomentumZ
declarations.doc: The z-component of the angular momentum is a smooth function on phase space.
declarations.statement: lemma contDiff_angularMomentumZ : ContDiff ℝ ∞ (Function.uncurry angularMomentumZ)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.hasGradientAt_angularMomentumSq_momentum
declarations.doc: The momentum gradient of `L²` is `2 ⟪q, q⟫ p - 2 ⟪q, p⟫ q`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasGradientAt_angularMomentumSq_momentum (p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :
    HasGradientAt (fun p' => angularMomentumSq p' q)
      ((2 * ⟪q, q⟫_ℝ) • p - (2 * ⟪q, p⟫_ℝ) • q) p

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.hasGradientAt_angularMomentumSq_position
declarations.doc: The position gradient of `L²` is `2 ⟪p, p⟫ q - 2 ⟪q, p⟫ p`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasGradientAt_angularMomentumSq_position (p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :
    HasGradientAt (fun q' => angularMomentumSq p q')
      ((2 * ⟪p, p⟫_ℝ) • q - (2 * ⟪q, p⟫_ℝ) • p) q

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.hasGradientAt_angularMomentumZ_momentum
declarations.doc: The momentum gradient of `L_z` is `q₀ e₁ - q₁ e₀`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasGradientAt_angularMomentumZ_momentum (p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :
    HasGradientAt (fun p' => angularMomentumZ p' q)
      (q 0 • EuclideanSpace.single 1 1 - q 1 • EuclideanSpace.single 0 1) p

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.hasGradientAt_angularMomentumZ_position
declarations.doc: The position gradient of `L_z` is `p₁ e₀ - p₀ e₁`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasGradientAt_angularMomentumZ_position (p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :
    HasGradientAt (fun q' => angularMomentumZ p q')
      (p 1 • EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 - p 0 • EuclideanSpace.single 1 1) q

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.poissonBracket_angularMomentumSq_angularMomentumZ
declarations.doc: The squared magnitude of the angular momentum and its z-component are in involution.
declarations.statement:
lemma poissonBracket_angularMomentumSq_angularMomentumZ (p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :
    poissonBracket angularMomentumSq angularMomentumZ p q = 0

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.poissonBracket_angularMomentumSq_eq_zero_of_hasGradientAt
declarations.doc:
`L²` Poisson-commutes with any phase-space function whose momentum gradient is parallel to the
momentum and whose position gradient is parallel to the position.

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.poissonBracket_angularMomentumZ_eq_zero_of_hasGradientAt
declarations.doc:
`L_z` Poisson-commutes with any phase-space function whose momentum gradient is parallel to
the momentum and whose position gradient is parallel to the position.

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.poissonBracket_angularMomentumSq_hamiltonian
declarations.doc:
Away from the centre of force, the squared magnitude of the angular momentum Poisson-commutes
with the Hamiltonian of a central-force system, so is conserved by the motion.
declarations.statement:
lemma poissonBracket_angularMomentumSq_hamiltonian (p : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))
    {q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)} (hq : q ≠ 0) :
    poissonBracket angularMomentumSq S.hamiltonian p q = 0

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.poissonBracket_angularMomentumZ_hamiltonian
declarations.doc:
Away from the centre of force, the z-component of the angular momentum Poisson-commutes with
the Hamiltonian of a central-force system, so is conserved by the motion.
declarations.statement:
lemma poissonBracket_angularMomentumZ_hamiltonian (p : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))
    {q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)} (hq : q ≠ 0) :
    poissonBracket angularMomentumZ S.hamiltonian p q = 0

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.hamiltonian_angularMomentumZ_eq_on_Icc
declarations.doc:
The energy and signed axial angular momentum agree at any two times on a central-force
trajectory satisfying Hamilton's equations away from the centre.
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonian_angularMomentumZ_eq_on_Icc
    {p q : ℝ → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)} {a b t₁ t₂ : ℝ}
    (h₁ : t₁ ∈ Set.Icc a b) (h₂ : t₂ ∈ Set.Icc a b)
    (hne : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc a b, q t ≠ 0)
    (hp : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc a b, HasDerivAt p (-(deriv S.V ‖q t‖ / ‖q t‖) • q t) t)
    (hq : ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc a b, HasDerivAt q (S.m⁻¹ • p t) t) :
    S.hamiltonian (p t₁) (q t₁) = S.hamiltonian (p t₂) (q t₂) ∧
    angularMomentumZ (p t₁) (q t₁) = angularMomentumZ (p t₂) (q t₂)

modules.title: Central forces
modules.doc:
Hamiltonian and partial gradients of a particle in a conservative central potential.

## i. Overview

This file models a particle of mass `m` in three-dimensional space under a conservative central
force centred at the origin. The force is derived from a potential `V (‖q‖)` which depends only on
the distance `‖q‖` from the origin. Its Hamiltonian, as a function of the momentum `p` and the
position `q`, is

$$H(p, q) = \frac{\langle p, p\rangle}{2m} + V(\|q\|).$$

The Kepler problem, `V r = -k / r`, and the isotropic harmonic oscillator, `V r = k r² / 2`, are
the most important examples.

The radial potential `V` is represented by a function on all of `ℝ`, with smoothness required
only for positive radii. Its value at zero is part of this total-function representation; the
position-gradient and smoothness results apply only when `q ≠ 0`, allowing potentials singular
at the physical centre.

This file defines the Hamiltonian and computes its partial gradients: the momentum gradient is the
velocity `p / m`, and away from the centre the position gradient `V'(‖q‖) q / ‖q‖` is parallel to
the position. The latter is what makes the angular momentum a conserved quantity.

## ii. Key results

- `CentralForce` : the input data, a mass and a potential smooth away from the centre of force.
- `CentralForce.hamiltonian` : the Hamiltonian.
- `CentralForce.hasGradientAt_hamiltonian_momentum`,
  `CentralForce.hasGradientAt_hamiltonian_position` : its partial gradients.
- `CentralForce.contDiffOn_hamiltonian` : it is smooth away from the centre of force.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The input data
- B. The Hamiltonian
  - B.1. Gradients of the Hamiltonian
  - B.2. Smoothness of the Hamiltonian
  - B.3. The Hamiltonian system

## iv. References

* H. Goldstein, C. Poole and J. Safko, *Classical Mechanics*, 3rd edition, Chapter 3.

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce
declarations.doc:
A particle in three-dimensional space under a conservative central force centred at the origin,
specified by its mass `m` and a radial potential `V` smooth at positive radii.
declarations.statement:
structure CentralForce where
  /-- The mass of the particle. -/
  m : ℝ
  /-- The potential, as a function of the distance from the centre of force. -/
  V : ℝ → ℝ
  /-- The mass of the particle is positive. -/
  m_pos : 0 < m
  /-- The potential is smooth away from the centre of force. -/
  contDiffOn_V : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ V (Set.Ioi 0)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.m_ne_zero
declarations.doc: The mass of the particle is non-zero.
declarations.statement: lemma m_ne_zero : S.m ≠ 0

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.hamiltonian
declarations.doc:
The Hamiltonian `H(p, q) = ⟪p, p⟫ / (2 m) + V ‖q‖` of a central-force system, as a function of
the momentum `p` and the position `q`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def hamiltonian (p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) : ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.hasGradientAt_hamiltonian_momentum
declarations.doc: The momentum gradient of the Hamiltonian of a central-force system is the velocity `p / m`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasGradientAt_hamiltonian_momentum (p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :
    HasGradientAt (fun p' => S.hamiltonian p' q) (S.m⁻¹ • p) p

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.hasGradientAt_hamiltonian_position
declarations.doc:
Away from the centre of force, the position gradient of the Hamiltonian of a central-force
system is `V'(‖q‖) q / ‖q‖`, which is parallel to the position.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasGradientAt_hamiltonian_position (p : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))
    {q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)} (hq : q ≠ 0) :
    HasGradientAt (fun q' => S.hamiltonian p q') ((deriv S.V ‖q‖ / ‖q‖) • q) q

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.contDiffOn_hamiltonian
declarations.doc: The Hamiltonian of a central-force system is smooth away from the centre of force.
declarations.statement:
lemma contDiffOn_hamiltonian :
    ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (Function.uncurry S.hamiltonian) {x | x.2 ≠ 0}

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.toHamiltonianSystem
declarations.doc: The Hamiltonian system of a central force, defined away from the centre of force.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toHamiltonianSystem :
    HamiltonianSystem 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) ⟨EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)⟩

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.mem_domain_toHamiltonianSystem
declarations.doc: A coordinate state belongs to the central-force domain exactly when its position is nonzero.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_domain_toHamiltonianSystem (p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :
    PhaseSpace.ofInnerProductSpace p q ∈ S.toHamiltonianSystem.domain ↔ q ≠ 0

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.toHamiltonianSystem_hamiltonian
declarations.doc: The bundled central-force system has the existing central-force Hamiltonian in coordinates.
declarations.statement:
lemma toHamiltonianSystem_hamiltonian (t : Time) (p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :
    S.toHamiltonianSystem.hamiltonian (t, PhaseSpace.ofInnerProductSpace p q) =
      S.hamiltonian p q

modules.title: Conserved quantities for central forces
modules.doc:
The Hamiltonian, squared angular momentum, and axial angular momentum as a family of observables.

## i. Overview

The central-force Hamiltonian and the squared magnitude and axial component of angular momentum
form a family of three observables. Their Poisson brackets vanish away from the centre of force,
and their phase-space gradients are given by the existing central-force results.

## ii. Key results

- `CentralForce.conservedQuantities` : the three observables.
- `CentralForce.poissonBracket_conservedQuantities` : the observables are pairwise in involution.
- `CentralForce.gradient_conservedQuantities` : the phase-space gradients of the observables.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The conserved quantities
  - A.1. Involution
  - A.2. Gradients

## iv. References

See `PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.AngularMomentum` for references.

sections.text: ## A. The conserved quantities
### A.1. Involution
### A.2. Gradients

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.conservedQuantities
declarations.doc:
The three conserved quantities in involution of a central-force system: the Hamiltonian `H`,
the squared magnitude `L²` of the angular momentum, and its z-component `L_z`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def conservedQuantities :
    Fin 3 → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) → ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.poissonBracket_conservedQuantities
declarations.doc:
Away from the centre of force, the conserved quantities of a central-force system are pairwise
in involution.
declarations.statement:
lemma poissonBracket_conservedQuantities (i j : Fin 3) (p : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))
    {q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)} (hq : q ≠ 0) :
    poissonBracket (S.conservedQuantities i) (S.conservedQuantities j) p q = 0

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.gradient_conservedQuantities
declarations.doc:
Away from the centre of force, the phase-space gradients of the conserved quantities of a
central-force system.
declarations.statement:
lemma gradient_conservedQuantities (p : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) {q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)}
    (hq : q ≠ 0) :
    (fun i => (gradient (fun p' => S.conservedQuantities i p' q) p,
      gradient (fun q' => S.conservedQuantities i p q') q)) =
    ![(S.m⁻¹ • p, (deriv S.V ‖q‖ / ‖q‖) • q),
      ((2 * ⟪q, q⟫_ℝ) • p - (2 * ⟪q, p⟫_ℝ) • q, (2 * ⟪p, p⟫_ℝ) • q - (2 * ⟪q, p⟫_ℝ) • p),
      (q 0 • EuclideanSpace.single 1 1 - q 1 • EuclideanSpace.single 0 1,
        p 1 • EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 - p 0 • EuclideanSpace.single 1 1)]

modules.title: Central-force systems are Liouville integrable
modules.doc:
Independence and involution of the Hamiltonian, squared angular momentum and axial component.

## i. Overview

The Hamiltonian `H`, squared angular momentum `L²` and axial component `L_z` are independent
and in involution on the open dense domain where the radial momentum is non-zero and the
angular momentum is not parallel to the z-axis. This proves Liouville integrability for every
central-force system. The domain is sufficient; no maximality claim is made.

Independence follows by pairing a vanishing combination of gradients with radial changes of
momentum, infinitesimal rotations and momentum scaling, successively eliminating its coefficients.

## ii. Key results

- `CentralForce.integrabilityDomain` : the chosen domain in phase space.
- `CentralForce.isOpen_integrabilityDomain`, `CentralForce.dense_integrabilityDomain` : it is
  open and dense.
- `CentralForce.snd_ne_zero_of_mem_integrabilityDomain` : it excludes the centre of force.
- `CentralForce.linearIndependent_conservedQuantities` : the observables are independent there.
- `CentralForce.liouvilleIntegrable` : the resulting Liouville-integrability construction.
- `CentralForce.toHamiltonianSystem_isLiouvilleIntegrableOn` : the shared Hamiltonian system is
  integrable on the same coordinate domain.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The domain of integrability
- B. Functional independence
- C. Liouville integrability

## iv. References

* V. I. Arnold, *Mathematical Methods of Classical Mechanics*, 2nd edition,
  Chapter 10. [ref: arnold_mechanics]

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.integrabilityDomain
declarations.doc:
The phase-space domain where the radial momentum is non-zero and the angular momentum
is not parallel to the z-axis, used to establish central-force integrability.
declarations.statement: def integrabilityDomain : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.integrabilityDomain_eq
declarations.doc: The domain is the non-vanishing set of a polynomial in the phase-space coordinates.

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.isOpen_integrabilityDomain
declarations.doc: The chosen central-force domain is open.
declarations.statement: lemma isOpen_integrabilityDomain : IsOpen integrabilityDomain

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.dense_integrabilityDomain
declarations.doc: The chosen central-force domain is dense.
declarations.statement: lemma dense_integrabilityDomain : Dense integrabilityDomain

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.snd_ne_zero_of_mem_integrabilityDomain
declarations.doc: The chosen domain excludes the centre of force.
declarations.statement:
lemma snd_ne_zero_of_mem_integrabilityDomain
    {x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)} (hx : x ∈ integrabilityDomain) :
    x.2 ≠ 0

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.linearIndependent_gradients
declarations.doc:
On the domain of integrability, a phase-space function whose momentum gradient is a non-zero
multiple `a • p` of the momentum and whose position gradient is a multiple `c • q` of the
position, such as the Hamiltonian of a central-force system, is functionally independent of `L²`
and `L_z`: the three phase-space gradients are linearly independent.
declarations.statement:
lemma linearIndependent_gradients {p q : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)} {a c : ℝ} (ha : a ≠ 0)
    (hx : (p, q) ∈ integrabilityDomain) :
    LinearIndependent ℝ ![(a • p, c • q),
      ((2 * ⟪q, q⟫_ℝ) • p - (2 * ⟪q, p⟫_ℝ) • q, (2 * ⟪p, p⟫_ℝ) • q - (2 * ⟪q, p⟫_ℝ) • p),
      (q 0 • EuclideanSpace.single 1 1 - q 1 • EuclideanSpace.single 0 1,
        p 1 • EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 - p 0 • EuclideanSpace.single 1 1)]

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.linearIndependent_conservedQuantities
declarations.doc:
On the domain of integrability, the conserved quantities of a central-force system are
functionally independent: their phase-space gradients are linearly independent.
declarations.statement:
lemma linearIndependent_conservedQuantities
    {x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)} (hx : x ∈ integrabilityDomain) :
    LinearIndependent ℝ (fun i => (gradient (fun p' => S.conservedQuantities i p' x.2) x.1,
      gradient (fun q' => S.conservedQuantities i x.1 q') x.2))

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.liouvilleIntegrable
declarations.doc:
Every central-force system is Liouville integrable on the domain of integrability, with the
Hamiltonian, the squared magnitude of the angular momentum and its z-component as conserved
quantities.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def liouvilleIntegrable :
    LiouvilleIntegrableOn integrabilityDomain S.hamiltonian

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.CentralForce.toHamiltonianSystem_isLiouvilleIntegrableOn
declarations.doc:
The Hamiltonian system associated with a central force is Liouville integrable on the
coordinate domain of integrability.
declarations.statement:
lemma toHamiltonianSystem_isLiouvilleIntegrableOn :
    S.toHamiltonianSystem.IsLiouvilleIntegrableOn integrabilityDomain

modules.title: Coupled spring potential
modules.doc:
The coupled spring potential x₀² + x₀x₁ + x₁² has a local minimum at the origin.

## i. Overview

As a proof of concept, we use the second derivative test in
`PhyslibAlpha.Mathematics.PartialDerivativeTest`
to prove that the coupled spring potential
`U := fun x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) => (x 0)^2 + x 0 * x 1 + (x 1)^2`
has a local minimum at zero.

To apply the test we show the potential is analytic, that its gradient vanishes at the origin, and
that its second derivative quadratic map is positive definite there.

## ii. Key results

- `couplingPotential` : the potential energy of a pair of coupled springs.
- `couplingPotential_gradient_zero` : the gradient of the potential vanishes at the origin.
- `couplingPotential_posDef` : the second derivative quadratic map is positive definite at the
  origin.
- `coupled_spring_potential` : the coupled spring potential has a local minimum at zero.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The coupled spring potential
- B. Analyticity and derivatives
- C. The local minimum at the origin

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: couplingPotential
declarations.doc: The potential energy of a pair of coupled springs.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def couplingPotential (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) : ℝ

declarations.name: couplingPotential_analyticAt
declarations.statement:
lemma couplingPotential_analyticAt (z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2)) :
    AnalyticAt ℝ couplingPotential z

declarations.name: couplingPotential_hasFDerivAt

modules.title: Liouville integrable systems
modules.doc:
Liouville integrability on an open dense domain and conservation along Hamiltonian trajectories.

## i. Overview

A Hamiltonian system on a `2d`-dimensional phase space is *Liouville integrable* when it carries
`d` conserved quantities, one per degree of freedom, that are

- smooth,
- pairwise Poisson-commuting ("in involution"), and
- functionally independent, i.e. their phase-space gradients are linearly independent.

Functional independence need not hold at every point of phase space: the
gradient of the Hamiltonian of the harmonic oscillator vanishes at the equilibrium, and the Kepler
Hamiltonian is singular at the origin of position space. The definition therefore asks for the
conditions on an open *domain* `U` of phase space, which must be dense so that the conditions hold
generically. Without density the empty domain would make every Hamiltonian integrable.

These are the integrability conditions used in the Liouville–Arnold theorem. Its conclusions about
invariant tori and action-angle coordinates require further hypotheses on common level sets and
are not formalized here (see the `TODO` below). What is formalized is the definition itself and its
consequence: each of the `d` conserved quantities really is conserved along the Hamiltonian flow
inside `U`, by reducing to `deriv_comp_eq_poissonBracket` from
`Physlib.ClassicalMechanics.HamiltonianMechanics.PoissonBracket`.

With one degree of freedom the conditions collapse: the Hamiltonian is the only conserved quantity,
involution is automatic, and independence says only that the gradient of the Hamiltonian does not
vanish. `LiouvilleIntegrableOn.oneDegreeOfFreedom` records this, and is how the harmonic oscillator
and the simple pendulum are shown to be integrable.

Following the convention of `poissonBracket`, a phase-space function `f : X → X → ℝ` is read as
`f p q` for a momentum `p` and a position `q`. Since PhysLib has no existing precedent for a
`FiniteDimensional`/`Module.finrank` hypothesis on an abstract phase space, position space is fixed
concretely as `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)` for an explicit `d : ℕ`, matching the indexing convention
already used for e.g. `RigidBody (d : ℕ)`.

## ii. Key results

- `LiouvilleIntegrableOn` : the structure of a Liouville integrable system for a Hamiltonian `H`
  on an open dense domain `U` of phase space.
- `HamiltonianSystem.LiouvilleIntegrabilityData` : an autonomous coordinate Hamiltonian and its
  integrability data, related to a Hamiltonian system on a coordinate domain.
- `HamiltonianSystem.IsLiouvilleIntegrableOn` : coordinate integrability for a Hamiltonian system,
  including agreement with an autonomous Hamiltonian on the integrability domain.
- `LiouvilleIntegrableOn.deriv_comp_eq_zero` : each conserved quantity has zero time derivative
  along a solution of Hamilton's equations for `H` which stays in `U`.
- `LiouvilleIntegrableOn.oneDegreeOfFreedom` : a system with one degree of freedom is Liouville
  integrable wherever its Hamiltonian is smooth with non-vanishing gradient.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The definition of Liouville integrability
  - A.1. Integrability of Hamiltonian systems
- B. Conservation along the flow
- C. Systems with one degree of freedom

## iv. References

* V. I. Arnold, *Mathematical Methods of Classical Mechanics*, 2nd edition, Chapter 10.

sections.text: ## A. The definition of Liouville integrability
### A.1. Integrability of Hamiltonian systems
## B. Conservation along the flow
## C. Systems with one degree of freedom

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.LiouvilleIntegrableOn
declarations.doc:
A Liouville integrable system for a Hamiltonian `H` on an open dense domain `U` of the
`2d`-dimensional phase space `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)`, whose points
are read as `(p, q)`: `d` smooth conserved quantities, one per degree of freedom, that are pairwise
in involution and functionally independent at every point of `U`.
declarations.statement:
structure LiouvilleIntegrableOn {d : ℕ}
    (U : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)))
    (H : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ) where
  /-- The domain on which the system is integrable is open. -/
  isOpen : IsOpen U
  /-- The domain on which the system is integrable is dense, i.e. integrability holds
  generically. -/
  dense : Dense U
  /-- The `d` conserved quantities, one per degree of freedom. -/
  f : Fin d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ
  /-- The conserved quantities are smooth on `U`. -/
  contDiffOn : ∀ i, ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (Function.uncurry (f i)) U
  /-- The Hamiltonian itself is one of the conserved quantities. -/
  exists_hamiltonian : ∃ i, f i = H
  /-- The conserved quantities pairwise Poisson-commute on `U`, i.e. are in involution. -/
  involutive : ∀ i j, ∀ x ∈ U, poissonBracket (f i) (f j) x.1 x.2 = 0
  /-- The conserved quantities are functionally independent on `U`: their phase-space gradients
  (the `p`- and `q`-partials together) are linearly independent. -/
  independent : ∀ x ∈ U, LinearIndependent ℝ
    (fun i => (gradient (fun p' => f i p' x.2) x.1, gradient (fun q' => f i x.1 q') x.2))

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HamiltonianSystem.LiouvilleIntegrabilityData
declarations.doc:
An autonomous coordinate Hamiltonian and its Liouville integrability data, related to a
Hamiltonian system on a coordinate domain.
declarations.statement:
structure HamiltonianSystem.LiouvilleIntegrabilityData {d : ℕ}
    (S : HamiltonianSystem 𝓘(ℝ, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) ⟨EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)⟩)
    (U : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) where
  /-- The autonomous Hamiltonian in momentum-position coordinates. -/
  coordinateHamiltonian : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ
  /-- The system agrees with the coordinate Hamiltonian on the domain at every time. -/
  hamiltonian_eq : ∀ t p q, (p, q) ∈ U →
    S.hamiltonian (t, PhaseSpace.ofInnerProductSpace p q) = coordinateHamiltonian p q
  /-- Coordinate states in the integrability domain belong to the system's domain. -/
  domain_subset : ∀ p q, (p, q) ∈ U → PhaseSpace.ofInnerProductSpace p q ∈ S.domain
  /-- The coordinate Hamiltonian has the Liouville integrability data. -/
  integrable : LiouvilleIntegrableOn U coordinateHamiltonian

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HamiltonianSystem.IsLiouvilleIntegrableOn
declarations.doc:
A Hamiltonian system is Liouville integrable on a coordinate domain when that domain lies
inside the system's domain and, for every time, the system agrees there with an autonomous
coordinate Hamiltonian satisfying the Liouville integrability conditions.

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.LiouvilleIntegrableOn.deriv_comp_eq_zero
declarations.doc:
Each conserved quantity of a Liouville integrable system has zero time derivative along a
solution of Hamilton's equations for `H` which lies in the domain `U` at time `t`.

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.LiouvilleIntegrableOn.oneDegreeOfFreedom
declarations.doc:
A Hamiltonian system with one degree of freedom is Liouville integrable, with the Hamiltonian as
its single conserved quantity, on any open dense domain on which the Hamiltonian is smooth and has
non-vanishing phase-space gradient.
declarations.statement:
def LiouvilleIntegrableOn.oneDegreeOfFreedom
    {U : Set (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1) × EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1))}
    {H : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1) → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 1) → ℝ}
    (hU : IsOpen U) (hdense : Dense U) (hH : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ (Function.uncurry H) U)
    (hgrad : ∀ x ∈ U,
      (gradient (fun p' => H p' x.2) x.1, gradient (fun q' => H x.1 q') x.2) ≠ 0) :
    LiouvilleIntegrableOn U H

modules.title: Souriau's moment map on a symplectic vector space
modules.doc:
Souriau's moment map, cocycle and Noether theorem for affine actions on a symplectic space.

## i. Overview

Souriau (Structure des systèmes dynamiques, Dunod 1970, chapter 11) attaches to a Lie group `G`
acting on a symplectic manifold `V` by symplectomorphisms (a *dynamical group*) a *moment*
`μ : V → 𝔤*`, defined by `σ(Z_V(x)) = -∇[μ.Z]` for every `Z` in the Lie algebra (11.7). Two moments
differ by a constant (11.8 a); the moment is constant along the motions (Noether's theorem, 11.12);
and the moment fails to be equivariant for the coadjoint action by a *symplectic cocycle* `θ` whose
derivative `f` is a 2-form on `𝔤` satisfying `σ(Z_V)(Z'_V) = μ[Z, Z'] + f(Z)(Z')` (11.17 d) and the
cyclic identity (11.33). The cohomology class of `θ` is an invariant of the dynamical group; it is
zero when a `G`-invariant potential of `σ` exists (11.21) and for semisimple groups (11.27).

This file states and proves these results in the setting of Souriau's example (11.2): a real
finite-dimensional symplectic vector space `E` on which a real Lie algebra `𝔤` acts by *affine*
infinitesimally symplectic vector fields `Z_E(x) = A Z x + b Z` (the infinitesimal version of the
affine symplectomorphisms `x ↦ B x + C` of (10.12)). No manifold is involved: the moment is given
explicitly by `μ.Z (x) = -½ σ(A Z x, x) - σ(b Z, x)`, the cocycle by `f(Z)(Z') = σ(b Z, b Z')`, and
Noether's theorem is stated for a Hamiltonian flow on `E`.

All signs follow Souriau's printed conventions: the bracket of the Lie algebra is the one for which
`Z ↦ Z_E` is a homomorphism for the bracket `[Z, Z']_E = Z'_E ∘ Z_E - Z_E ∘ Z'_E` of (11.22 a)
(opposite to the usual commutator), `Ad(Z)(Z') = [Z, Z']` (6.13 b), and the coadjoint vector
field is `Z_{𝔤*}(ν) = ν ∘ Ad(Z)` (11.16).

## ii. Key results

- `AffineSymplecticAction.hasFDerivAt_moment`: (11.7), `σ(Z_E(x)) = -∇[μ.Z]`.
- `AffineSymplecticAction.moment_unique`: (11.8 a), two moments differ by a constant torsor; this is
  proved without the alternation of `σ`, from the symmetry of the second derivative of the given
  moment.
- `AffineSymplecticAction.sigma_vectorField_vectorField`: (11.17 d),
  `σ(Z_E)(Z'_E) = μ[Z, Z'] + f(Z)(Z')`.
- `AffineSymplecticAction.cocycle_cyclic`: (11.33), the cyclic identity of the symplectic cocycle.
- `AffineSymplecticAction.equivariant_of_coboundary`: (11.27) in this setting, a coboundary cocycle
  can be absorbed in the moment.
- `AffineSymplecticAction.noether`: (11.12), `μ.Z` is a first integral of every `Z_E`-invariant
  Hamiltonian flow.
- `planeTranslations_not_coboundary`: the translations of the plane have a non-zero cohomology class
  (the simplest instance of Souriau's "mass" cocycle).

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Symplectic forms
- B. Affine symplectic actions of a Lie algebra
- C. The Souriau cocycle
- D. The moment map
- E. Noether's theorem
- F. The plane: translations and a non-trivial cohomology class

## iv. References

- J.-M. Souriau, Structure des systèmes dynamiques, Dunod, Paris, 1970, chapter 11,
  pp. 104-117; English translation: Structure of Dynamical Systems, Birkhäuser, 1997
  (same equation numbers).

* J.-M. Souriau, *Structure des systèmes dynamiques*, Maîtrises de mathématiques, Dunod,
  Paris, 1970, chapter 11, pp. 104-117. The equation numbers (11.7),
  (11.8), (11.12), (11.17), (11.22), (11.27), (11.33) refer to this edition. [ref: Souriau1970]

sections.text:
## A. Symplectic forms

Souriau's "forme de Lagrange" `σ` is an alternating non-degenerate bilinear form.

## B. Affine symplectic actions of a Lie algebra

The infinitesimal version of Souriau's example (11.2) with the affine symplectomorphisms of (10.12):
each `Z` of the Lie algebra acts on `E` by the affine vector field `Z_E(x) = A Z x + b Z`, with
`A Z` infinitesimally symplectic ((10.28)-(10.32)), and the bracket is Souriau's (6.12 b),
(11.22 a): `[Z, Z']_E = Z'_E ∘ Z_E - Z_E ∘ Z'_E`, extended to affine vector fields by the formula
`[X, X'](x) = DX'(x)(X(x)) - DX(x)(X'(x))`.

## C. The Souriau cocycle

(11.17 d, ♯), (11.30), (11.33), the Lie algebra cocycle identity (11.22)/(11.24), the change of
moment (11.18), the coboundary case (11.27) and the linear case (11.21). Everything here is algebra:
only the bilinearity and the alternation of `σ` and the axioms of the action are used.

## D. The moment map

(11.7), (11.9) and (11.8 a), then the infinitesimal equivariance (11.17 d, ♠) and the identity
(11.8 c). The derivative of `y ↦ σ (A y) y` is computed by viewing `y ↦ σ (A y)` as a continuous
linear map into `E →L[ℝ] ℝ`.

## E. Noether's theorem

(11.12) states that a moment is constant on each leaf of the presymplectic evolution space. On `E`,
for a Hamiltonian flow `γ' = X ∘ γ` with `X` the symplectic gradient of an `H` invariant under
`Z_E`, this says that `μ.Z ∘ γ` is constant.

## F. The plane: translations and a non-trivial cohomology class

The standard symplectic form of `ℝ × ℝ` and the translations `x ↦ x + Z`, whose vector fields are
constant, `Z_E(x) = Z`: their cocycle is `σ(Z, Z')` itself, which is not a coboundary (the Lie
algebra is abelian, so every coboundary vanishes). This is the simplest instance of (11.20)-(11.21):
no invariant potential exists, and no moment of the translations is equivariant.

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.IsSymplecticForm
declarations.doc: A symplectic form on a real vector space: an alternating non-degenerate bilinear form.
declarations.statement:
structure IsSymplecticForm {E : Type} [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E] (σ : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ E) :
    Prop where
  /-- `σ` is alternating: `σ v v = 0`. -/
  alt : LinearMap.BilinForm.IsAlt σ
  /-- `σ` is non-degenerate. -/
  nondeg : LinearMap.BilinForm.Nondegenerate σ

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction
declarations.doc:
An affine infinitesimally symplectic action of a Lie algebra `g` on `E`, in Souriau's
conventions: `Z_E(x) = A Z x + b Z`.
declarations.statement:
structure AffineSymplecticAction {E : Type} [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E]
    (σ : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ E) (g : Type) [LieRing g] [LieAlgebra ℝ g] where
  /-- The linear part `Z ↦ A Z` of the vector fields. -/
  A : g →ₗ[ℝ] (E →ₗ[ℝ] E)
  /-- The constant part `Z ↦ b Z` of the vector fields. -/
  b : g →ₗ[ℝ] E
  /-- Each `A Z` is infinitesimally symplectic: `σ (A Z v) w + σ v (A Z w) = 0`. -/
  infinitesimallySymplectic : ∀ Z v w, σ (A Z v) w + σ v (A Z w) = 0
  /-- Souriau's bracket (11.22 a) on the linear parts: `A [Z, Z'] = A Z' ∘ A Z - A Z ∘ A Z'`. -/
  map_bracket_A : ∀ Z Z', A ⁅Z, Z'⁆ = A Z' ∘ₗ A Z - A Z ∘ₗ A Z'
  /-- Souriau's bracket on the constant parts: `b [Z, Z'] = A Z' (b Z) - A Z (b Z')`. -/
  map_bracket_b : ∀ Z Z', b ⁅Z, Z'⁆ = A Z' (b Z) - A Z (b Z')

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.coadjoint
declarations.doc:
(11.16) with (6.13 b): the coadjoint vector field `Z_{𝔤*}(ν) = ν ∘ Ad(Z)`,
`Ad(Z)(Z') = [Z, Z']`, for a torsor `ν` given as a function; this is also the coboundary
`δ(ν)(Z)` of (11.24).
declarations.statement: def coadjoint {g : Type} [LieRing g] (Z : g) (ν : g → ℝ) (Z' : g) : ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.vectorField
declarations.doc: (6.11): the affine vector field `Z_E` associated with `Z`.
declarations.statement: def vectorField (Z : g) (x : E) : E

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.moment
declarations.doc:
The moment (11.7), (11.9) of the action, as a function of the point `x` and of `Z`:
`μ.Z (x) = -½ σ(A Z x, x) - σ(b Z, x)`. Its sign is fixed by (11.7).
declarations.statement: def moment (x : E) (Z : g) : ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.cocycle
declarations.doc: (11.17 c): Souriau's cocycle `f(Z)(Z') = σ(b Z, b Z')`, a 2-form on `g`.
declarations.statement: def cocycle (Z Z' : g) : ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.sigma_A_left
declarations.doc: `infinitesimallySymplectic` in the form `σ (A Z v) w = -σ v (A Z w)`.
declarations.statement: lemma sigma_A_left (Z : g) (v w : E) : σ (ρ.A Z v) w = -σ v (ρ.A Z w)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.sigma_A_right
declarations.doc: `infinitesimallySymplectic` in the form `σ v (A Z w) = -σ (A Z v) w`.
declarations.statement: lemma sigma_A_right (Z : g) (v w : E) : σ v (ρ.A Z w) = -σ (ρ.A Z v) w

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.sigma_A_symm
declarations.doc: For an alternating `σ`, `σ (A Z v) w` is symmetric in `v`, `w`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sigma_A_symm (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ) (Z : g) (v w : E) :
    σ (ρ.A Z v) w = σ (ρ.A Z w) v

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.moment_add
declarations.doc: The moment is a torsor: `μ.(Z + Z') = μ.Z + μ.Z'`.
declarations.statement: lemma moment_add (x : E) (Z Z' : g) : ρ.moment x (Z + Z') = ρ.moment x Z + ρ.moment x Z'

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.moment_smul
declarations.doc: The moment is a torsor: `μ.(c Z) = c μ.Z`.
declarations.statement: lemma moment_smul (x : E) (c : ℝ) (Z : g) : ρ.moment x (c • Z) = c * ρ.moment x Z

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.sigma_vectorField_vectorField
declarations.statement:
lemma sigma_vectorField_vectorField (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ) (Z Z' : g) (x : E) :
    σ (ρ.vectorField Z x) (ρ.vectorField Z' x) = ρ.moment x ⁅Z, Z'⁆ + ρ.cocycle Z Z'

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.cocycle_antisymm
declarations.doc: (11.30): the cocycle is antisymmetric.
declarations.statement:
lemma cocycle_antisymm (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ) (Z Z' : g) :
    ρ.cocycle Z' Z = -ρ.cocycle Z Z'

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.cocycle_cyclic
declarations.statement:
lemma cocycle_cyclic (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ) (Z Z' Z'' : g) :
    ρ.cocycle Z ⁅Z', Z''⁆ + ρ.cocycle Z' ⁅Z'', Z⁆ + ρ.cocycle Z'' ⁅Z, Z'⁆ = 0

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.cocycle_lie
declarations.doc:
(11.22)/(11.24) for the coadjoint representation: `f` is a Lie algebra cocycle,
`f([Z, Z']) = Z'_{𝔤*}(f(Z)) - Z_{𝔤*}(f(Z'))`, evaluated on `Z''`.
declarations.statement:
lemma cocycle_lie (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ) (Z Z' Z'' : g) :
    ρ.cocycle ⁅Z, Z'⁆ Z'' = ρ.cocycle Z ⁅Z', Z''⁆ - ρ.cocycle Z' ⁅Z, Z''⁆

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.sigma_vectorField_vectorField_shift
declarations.doc:
(11.18): changing the moment into `μ - μ₀` (`μ₀` a constant torsor) keeps (11.17 d) with the
cocycle `f + Z_{𝔤*}(μ₀)`, i.e. `f(Z)(Z') + μ₀ [Z, Z']`.
declarations.statement:
lemma sigma_vectorField_vectorField_shift (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ) (μ₀ : Dual ℝ g) (Z Z' : g)
    (x : E) :
    σ (ρ.vectorField Z x) (ρ.vectorField Z' x) =
      (ρ.moment x ⁅Z, Z'⁆ - μ₀ ⁅Z, Z'⁆) + (ρ.cocycle Z Z' + coadjoint Z μ₀ Z')

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.equivariant_of_coboundary
declarations.doc:
(11.27) in this setting: if the cocycle is a coboundary, `f(Z)(Z') = μ₀ [Z, Z']`, then the
moment `μ + μ₀` is exactly equivariant.
declarations.statement:
lemma equivariant_of_coboundary (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ) (μ₀ : Dual ℝ g)
    (h : ∀ Z Z', ρ.cocycle Z Z' = coadjoint Z μ₀ Z') (Z Z' : g) (x : E) :
    σ (ρ.vectorField Z x) (ρ.vectorField Z' x) = ρ.moment x ⁅Z, Z'⁆ + μ₀ ⁅Z, Z'⁆

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.cocycle_eq_zero_of_linear
declarations.doc:
(11.21) in this setting: a linear action (`b = 0`, the case (11.2) of `Sp(E)`) has a zero
cocycle.
declarations.statement: lemma cocycle_eq_zero_of_linear (hb : ρ.b = 0) (Z Z' : g) : ρ.cocycle Z Z' = 0

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.IsSymplecticGradient
declarations.doc:
The symplectic gradient (9.16) in the convention of (11.7) and (10.32): `X` is the symplectic
gradient of `u` when `σ (X x) v = -Du(x)(v)` for all `x`, `v`.
declarations.statement:
def IsSymplecticGradient {E : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    (σ : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ E) (u : E → ℝ) (X : E → E) : Prop

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.sigmaA
declarations.doc: `y ↦ σ (A Z y)` as a continuous linear map from `E` to `E →L[ℝ] ℝ`.
declarations.statement: def sigmaA (Z : g) : E →L[ℝ] (E →L[ℝ] ℝ)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.sigmaA_apply
declarations.statement: lemma sigmaA_apply (Z : g) (y v : E) : ρ.sigmaA Z y v = σ (ρ.A Z y) v

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.sigmaB
declarations.doc: The constant linear form `σ (b Z)` as a continuous linear map.
declarations.statement: def sigmaB (Z : g) : E →L[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.sigmaB_apply
declarations.statement: lemma sigmaB_apply (Z : g) (v : E) : ρ.sigmaB Z v = σ (ρ.b Z) v

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.hasFDerivAt_quad
declarations.doc: The derivative of `y ↦ σ (A Z y) y` at `x` is `v ↦ σ (A Z v) x + σ (A Z x) v`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasFDerivAt_quad (Z : g) (x : E) :
    HasFDerivAt (fun y => σ (ρ.A Z y) y)
      ((ρ.sigmaA Z x).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ E) + (ρ.sigmaA Z).flip x) x

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.hasFDerivAt_moment_of_symm
declarations.doc: (11.7) under the sole symmetry `σ (A Z v) w = σ (A Z w) v`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasFDerivAt_moment_of_symm (Z : g) (hsym : ∀ v w, σ (ρ.A Z v) w = σ (ρ.A Z w) v) (x : E) :
    HasFDerivAt (fun y => ρ.moment y Z)
      (-(LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (σ (ρ.vectorField Z x)))) x

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.hasFDerivAt_moment
declarations.doc: (11.7): `σ(Z_E(x)) = -∇[μ.Z]`, the derivative of `x ↦ μ.Z` at `x` is `v ↦ -σ (Z_E x) v`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasFDerivAt_moment (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ) (Z : g) (x : E) :
    HasFDerivAt (fun y => ρ.moment y Z)
      (-(LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (σ (ρ.vectorField Z x)))) x

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.vectorField_isSymplecticGradient
declarations.doc: (11.9): `Z_E` is the symplectic gradient of `μ.Z`.
declarations.statement:
lemma vectorField_isSymplecticGradient (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ) (Z : g) :
    IsSymplecticGradient σ (fun y => ρ.moment y Z) (ρ.vectorField Z)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.hasFDerivAt_negSigmaVectorField
declarations.doc: The derivative of the affine map `x ↦ -σ (Z_E x)` (with values in `E →L[ℝ] ℝ`) is `-sigmaA`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasFDerivAt_negSigmaVectorField (Z : g) (x : E) :
    HasFDerivAt (fun y => -(LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (σ (ρ.vectorField Z y))))
      (-(ρ.sigmaA Z)) x

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.moment_unique
declarations.doc:
(11.8 a): two moments of the same action differ by a constant torsor (`E` is connected). Any `ψ`
satisfying (11.7) equals `μ + c`, `Z` by `Z`. No alternation of `σ` is needed: the symmetry of the
second derivative of `ψ` gives `σ (A Z v) w = σ (A Z w) v`.
declarations.statement:
lemma moment_unique (ψ : E → g → ℝ)
    (hψ : ∀ Z x, HasFDerivAt (fun y => ψ y Z)
      (-(LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (σ (ρ.vectorField Z x)))) x) (Z : g) :
    ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ x, ψ x Z = ρ.moment x Z + c

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.fderiv_moment_vectorField
declarations.doc:
(11.17 d, ♠): `D(ψ)(x)(Z_E(x)) = ψ(x).ad(Z) + f(Z)`, evaluated on `Z'`: the infinitesimal
equivariance of the moment, up to the cocycle.
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_moment_vectorField (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ) (Z Z' : g) (x : E) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun y => ρ.moment y Z') x (ρ.vectorField Z x) =
      coadjoint Z (ρ.moment x) Z' + ρ.cocycle Z Z'

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.sigma_vectorField_bracket
declarations.doc:
(11.8 c): `σ([Z, Z']_E(x)) = -∇[σ(Z_E(x))(Z'_E(x))]`, an identity valid for every dynamical
group.
declarations.statement:
lemma sigma_vectorField_bracket (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ) (Z Z' : g) (x v : E) :
    σ (ρ.vectorField ⁅Z, Z'⁆ x) v =
      -(fderiv ℝ (fun y => σ (ρ.vectorField Z y) (ρ.vectorField Z' y)) x v)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.noether
declarations.doc:
(11.12), Noether's theorem: along a motion of a Hamiltonian `H` invariant under `Z_E`, the
component `μ.Z` of the moment has zero derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma noether (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ) (H : E → ℝ) (X : E → E) (hX : IsSymplecticGradient σ H X)
    (Z : g) (hinv : ∀ x, fderiv ℝ H x (ρ.vectorField Z x) = 0)
    (γ : ℝ → E) (hγ : ∀ t, HasDerivAt γ (X (γ t)) t) (t : ℝ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun s => ρ.moment (γ s) Z) 0 t

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticAction.noether_const
declarations.doc: (11.12) as a conservation law: `μ.Z` takes the same value at any two instants of a motion.
declarations.statement:
lemma noether_const (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ) (H : E → ℝ) (X : E → E)
    (hX : IsSymplecticGradient σ H X) (Z : g) (hinv : ∀ x, fderiv ℝ H x (ρ.vectorField Z x) = 0)
    (γ : ℝ → E) (hγ : ∀ t, HasDerivAt γ (X (γ t)) t) (t s : ℝ) :
    ρ.moment (γ t) Z = ρ.moment (γ s) Z

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.instLieRingPlane
declarations.doc: `ℝ × ℝ` as an abelian Lie ring (the commutator bracket of the product ring, which vanishes).
declarations.statement: instance instLieRingPlane : LieRing (ℝ × ℝ)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.instLieAlgebraPlane
declarations.doc: `ℝ × ℝ` as an abelian real Lie algebra.
declarations.statement: instance instLieAlgebraPlane : LieAlgebra ℝ (ℝ × ℝ)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.planeForm
declarations.doc: The standard symplectic form of the plane, `σ((a, b), (c, d)) = a d - b c`.
declarations.statement: def planeForm : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ (ℝ × ℝ)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.planeTranslations
declarations.doc: The translations `x ↦ x + Z` of the plane: `A = 0`, `b = id`, so `Z_E(x) = Z`.
declarations.statement: def planeTranslations : AffineSymplecticAction planeForm (ℝ × ℝ)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.isSymplecticForm_planeForm
declarations.doc: `planeForm` is symplectic.
declarations.statement: lemma isSymplecticForm_planeForm : IsSymplecticForm planeForm

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.planeTranslations_cocycle
declarations.doc:
(11.17 c), (11.20): for the translations of the plane the cocycle is `σ(Z, Z')`, so
`f((1, 0))((0, 1)) = 1`.
declarations.statement: lemma planeTranslations_cocycle : planeTranslations.cocycle (1, 0) (0, 1) = 1

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.planeTranslations_not_coboundary
declarations.doc:
(11.21): the cocycle of the translations is not a coboundary: the cohomology class of the
translations of the plane is not zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma planeTranslations_not_coboundary :
    ¬ ∃ μ₀ : Dual ℝ (ℝ × ℝ), ∀ Z Z', planeTranslations.cocycle Z Z' = coadjoint Z μ₀ Z'

modules.title: The cohomology class of the affine symplectic group
modules.doc:
The moment cocycle of the affine symplectic group has a non-zero cohomology class.

## i. Overview

Souriau (Structure des systemes dynamiques, Dunod 1970, chapter 11) attaches to a dynamical group
`G` acting on a connected symplectic (or presymplectic) manifold `V` with moment `μ` a map
`θ : G → 𝔤*`, `θ(a) = μ(a_V(x)) - a_{𝔤*}(μ(x))` (11.17 a), which by connectedness does not depend
on `x` and satisfies the cocycle identity `θ(a × b) = θ(a) + a_{𝔤*}(θ(b))` (11.17 b). Its
cohomology class does not depend on the choice of the moment (11.18), (11.20), and it vanishes
when a `G`-invariant potential exists (11.21).

This file proves the following for the group of Souriau's example (10.12), the affine symplectic
group `Sp(E) ⋉ E` of a real symplectic vector space `E`, acting by `x ↦ B x + C`, with the moment
`moment` of (11.7): the defect `θ(a)` does not depend on `x` and equals `μ(C)` (a computation here,
not a consequence of connectedness), `θ` is a 1-cocycle of the coadjoint action, its derivative
at the identity along a curve is the Lie algebra cocycle of
`PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalMechanics.MomentMap.Basic`, and its cohomology class is not zero. It does NOT
prove (11.18), (11.20) or (11.21): by (11.21) the non-zero class means that no potential of `σ` is
invariant under this group, but that implication is Souriau's and is not formalised here.

The Lie algebra is the space of pairs `(A, b)` with `A` infinitesimally symplectic, acting by the
affine vector fields `Z_E(x) = A x + b`; only its module structure is used, and no Lean term
relates it to `AffineSymplecticAction` (the link with its cocycle is by formula). The adjoint
action is given by the formula of `adjoint` and characterised by the identity `vectorField_adjoint`
of (6.25); the coadjoint action `a_{𝔤*}(μ) = μ ∘ Ad(a⁻¹)` of (11.15) is a `MulAction` on the
dual.

The cocycle notions are Mathlib's: `θ` is a `groupCohomology.IsCocycle₁` for the coadjoint action,
and "the class is non-zero" is `¬ groupCohomology.IsCoboundary₁`. Souriau's differentiability
requirement on `θ` is not formalised: the group here carries no manifold structure, and `θ` is
given by a closed formula.

## ii. Key results

- `vectorField_adjoint`: (6.25), `(Ad(a) Z)_E (a_E x) = B (Z_E x)`, which characterises `adjoint`
  together with `vectorField_injective`.
- `moment_smul_sub_smul_moment`: (11.17 a) in closed form, `μ(a_E(x)) - a_{𝔤*}(μ(x)) = μ(C)`: the
  defect `θ(a)` does not depend on `x`, and is the moment at the point `a_E(0) = C`.
- `isCocycle₁_moment_translation`: (11.17 b), `θ` is a 1-cocycle of the coadjoint action.
- `hasDerivAt_moment_translation`: part of (11.17 c), the derivative of `θ` at the identity along a
  curve whose translation part has velocity `b'` is `σ (b', b Z)`, the value of
  `AffineSymplecticAction.cocycle` (the 2-form property and ♣ of (11.17 c) are not proved here).
- `not_isCoboundary₁_moment_translation`: the cohomology class of the affine symplectic group is
  non-zero as soon as `E ≠ 0`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The affine symplectic group
- B. Its Lie algebra and the adjoint action
- C. The coadjoint action and the moment
- D. The cohomology class
- E. The plane

## iv. References

- J.-M. Souriau, Structure des systemes dynamiques, Dunod, Paris, 1970: chapter 11,
  pp. 104-117, for (11.7), (11.15)-(11.21) and (11.28); (6.24)-(6.25) and (10.12),
  (10.28)-(10.32) for the adjoint action and the affine symplectic group.

* J.-M. Souriau, *Structure des systèmes dynamiques*, Maîtrises de mathématiques, Dunod,
  Paris, 1970, chapter 11, pp. 104-117, and (6.24)-(6.25), (10.12). The
  equation numbers refer to this edition. [ref: Souriau1970]

sections.text:
## A. The affine symplectic group

The affine symplectomorphisms `x ↦ B x + C` of (10.12), with `B` linear symplectic.

## B. Its Lie algebra and the adjoint action

The pairs `(A, b)` with `A` infinitesimally symplectic, acting by the affine vector fields
`Z_E(x) = A x + b` of `AffineSymplecticAction`; the adjoint action of (6.24) is characterised by
(6.25). Only the module structure is used here: the Lie bracket of Souriau's (11.22 a) lives on
the abstract Lie algebra of `AffineSymplecticAction`.

## C. The coadjoint action and the moment

The coadjoint action of (11.15), `a_{𝔤*}(μ) = μ ∘ Ad(a⁻¹)`, and the moment of (11.7), which is the
moment of `AffineSymplecticAction` read on the pairs `(A, b)`.

## D. The cohomology class

(11.17 a) in closed form, (11.17 b), (11.17 c) and the non-vanishing of the class.

## E. The plane

The simplest instance: the standard symplectic plane, whose affine symplectic group has a non-zero
cohomology class. This is the group-level counterpart of `planeTranslations_not_coboundary`.

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticGroup
declarations.doc:
The affine symplectic group of a bilinear form `σ` on `E`: the affine maps `x ↦ B x + C` with
`B` a linear equivalence preserving `σ` (Souriau (10.12)).
declarations.statement:
structure AffineSymplecticGroup {E : Type} [AddCommGroup E] [Module ℝ E]
    (σ : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ E) where
  /-- The linear part `B`. -/
  linear : E ≃ₗ[ℝ] E
  /-- The translation part `C`. -/
  translation : E
  /-- The linear part preserves `σ`. -/
  map_symplecticForm : ∀ v w, σ (linear v) (linear w) = σ v w
instance : Mul (AffineSymplecticGroup σ)
instance : One (AffineSymplecticGroup σ)
instance : Inv (AffineSymplecticGroup σ)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticGroup.mul_linear
declarations.statement: lemma mul_linear (a b : AffineSymplecticGroup σ) : (a * b).linear = b.linear.trans a.linear

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticGroup.mul_translation
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_translation (a b : AffineSymplecticGroup σ) :
    (a * b).translation = a.linear b.translation + a.translation

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticGroup.one_linear
declarations.statement: lemma one_linear : (1 : AffineSymplecticGroup σ).linear = LinearEquiv.refl ℝ E

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticGroup.one_translation
declarations.statement: lemma one_translation : (1 : AffineSymplecticGroup σ).translation = 0

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticGroup.inv_linear
declarations.statement: lemma inv_linear (a : AffineSymplecticGroup σ) : a⁻¹.linear = a.linear.symm

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticGroup.inv_translation
declarations.statement:
lemma inv_translation (a : AffineSymplecticGroup σ) :
    a⁻¹.translation = -(a.linear.symm a.translation)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticGroup.ext
declarations.doc: Two elements with the same linear and translation parts are equal.
declarations.statement:
lemma ext {a b : AffineSymplecticGroup σ} (hl : a.linear = b.linear)
    (ht : a.translation = b.translation) : a = b
instance : Group (AffineSymplecticGroup σ)

declarations.doc: The affine symplectic group acts on `E` by `a_E(x) = B x + C` (10.12).
declarations.statement: instance : MulAction (AffineSymplecticGroup σ) E

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.AffineSymplecticGroup.smul_def
declarations.statement: lemma smul_def (a : AffineSymplecticGroup σ) (x : E) : a • x = a.linear x + a.translation

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.affineSymplecticAlgebra
declarations.doc:
The Lie algebra of the affine symplectic group: the pairs `(A, b)` with `A` infinitesimally
symplectic ((10.28)-(10.32)).
declarations.statement: def affineSymplecticAlgebra (σ : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ E) : Submodule ℝ ((E →ₗ[ℝ] E) × E)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.mem_affineSymplecticAlgebra
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_affineSymplecticAlgebra {Z : (E →ₗ[ℝ] E) × E} :
    Z ∈ affineSymplecticAlgebra σ ↔ ∀ v w, σ (Z.1 v) w + σ v (Z.1 w) = 0

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.vectorField
declarations.doc: The affine vector field `Z_E(x) = A x + b` of `Z = (A, b)`, as in `AffineSymplecticAction`.
declarations.statement: def vectorField (Z : affineSymplecticAlgebra σ) (x : E) : E

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.adjoint
declarations.doc: The adjoint action (6.24): `Ad(a)(A, b) = (B A B⁻¹, B b - B A B⁻¹ C)` for `a = (B, C)`.
declarations.statement:
def adjoint (a : AffineSymplecticGroup σ) :
    affineSymplecticAlgebra σ →ₗ[ℝ] affineSymplecticAlgebra σ

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.adjoint_one
declarations.statement: lemma adjoint_one : adjoint (1 : AffineSymplecticGroup σ) = LinearMap.id

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.adjoint_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma adjoint_mul (a b : AffineSymplecticGroup σ) :
    adjoint (a * b) = adjoint a ∘ₗ adjoint b

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.vectorField_adjoint
declarations.doc:
(6.25): the adjoint action is the one for which `(Ad(a) Z)_E (a_E x) = B (Z_E x)`. With
`vectorField_injective` this characterises `adjoint`.
declarations.statement:
lemma vectorField_adjoint (a : AffineSymplecticGroup σ) (Z : affineSymplecticAlgebra σ) (x : E) :
    vectorField (adjoint a Z) (a • x) = a.linear (vectorField Z x)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.vectorField_injective
declarations.doc: An element of the Lie algebra is determined by its vector field.
declarations.statement:
lemma vectorField_injective {Z Z' : affineSymplecticAlgebra σ}
    (h : ∀ x, vectorField Z x = vectorField Z' x) : Z = Z'

declarations.doc: (11.15): the coadjoint action `a_{𝔤*}(μ) = μ.a_𝔤⁻¹`, that is `μ ∘ Ad(a⁻¹)`.
declarations.statement: instance : SMul (AffineSymplecticGroup σ) (Dual ℝ (affineSymplecticAlgebra σ))

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.coadjoint_smul_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma coadjoint_smul_apply (a : AffineSymplecticGroup σ) (μ : Dual ℝ (affineSymplecticAlgebra σ))
    (Z : affineSymplecticAlgebra σ) : (a • μ) Z = μ (adjoint a⁻¹ Z)
instance : MulAction (AffineSymplecticGroup σ) (Dual ℝ (affineSymplecticAlgebra σ))
instance : DistribMulAction (AffineSymplecticGroup σ) (Dual ℝ (affineSymplecticAlgebra σ))

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.moment
declarations.doc:
(11.7): the moment of the affine symplectic action, `μ(x)(A, b) = -½ σ(A x, x) - σ(b, x)`, the
moment of `AffineSymplecticAction` read on the pairs `(A, b)`.
declarations.statement: def moment (σ : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ E) (x : E) : Dual ℝ (affineSymplecticAlgebra σ)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.moment_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma moment_apply (x : E) (Z : affineSymplecticAlgebra σ) :
    moment σ x Z = -(1 / 2 : ℝ) * σ (Z.1.1 x) x - σ Z.1.2 x

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.moment_zero
declarations.statement: lemma moment_zero : moment σ (0 : E) = 0

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.moment_smul_sub_smul_moment
declarations.doc:
(11.17 a) in closed form: for this moment, the defect `θ(a) = μ(a_E(x)) - a_{𝔤*}(μ(x))` does
not depend on the point `x`, and equals the moment at `a_E(0) = C`. The terms in `x` cancel by the
infinitesimal symplecticity of `A` and the alternation of `σ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma moment_smul_sub_smul_moment (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ) (x : E)
    (a : AffineSymplecticGroup σ) :
    moment σ (a • x) - a • moment σ x = moment σ a.translation

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.isCocycle₁_moment_translation
declarations.doc:
(11.17 b): `θ(a) = μ(C)` is a 1-cocycle of the coadjoint action,
`θ(a × b) = θ(a) + a_{𝔤*}(θ(b))`.
declarations.statement:
lemma isCocycle₁_moment_translation (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ) :
    groupCohomology.IsCocycle₁ (fun a : AffineSymplecticGroup σ => moment σ a.translation)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.sigmaLinear
declarations.doc:
`y ↦ σ (A y)` as a continuous linear map from `E` to `E →L[ℝ] ℝ`, used to differentiate the
quadratic part of the moment.
declarations.statement:
def sigmaLinear {E : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
    (σ : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ E) (A : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) : E →L[ℝ] (E →L[ℝ] ℝ)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.sigmaLinear_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma sigmaLinear_apply {E : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (σ : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ E) (A : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) (y v : E) :
    sigmaLinear σ A y v = σ (A y) v

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.hasFDerivAt_quad
declarations.doc: The derivative of `y ↦ σ (A y) y` at `x` is `v ↦ σ (A v) x + σ (A x) v`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasFDerivAt_quad {E : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] (σ : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ E) (A : E →ₗ[ℝ] E) (x : E) :
    HasFDerivAt (fun y => σ (A y) y)
      ((sigmaLinear σ A x).comp (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ E) + (sigmaLinear σ A).flip x) x

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.hasFDerivAt_moment
declarations.doc: (11.7) for the affine symplectic group: `σ(Z_E(x)) = -∇[μ.Z]`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasFDerivAt_moment {E : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {σ : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ E} (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ)
    (Z : affineSymplecticAlgebra σ) (x : E) :
    HasFDerivAt (fun y => moment σ y Z)
      (-(LinearMap.toContinuousLinearMap (σ (vectorField Z x)))) x

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.hasDerivAt_moment_translation
declarations.doc:
Part of (11.17 c): along any curve of the group issued from the identity whose translation part
has velocity `b'`, the derivative of `θ = μ(C)` at the identity is `σ (b', b Z)`, which is the value
of `AffineSymplecticAction.cocycle` on the corresponding pairs (a relation by formula: no Lean term
relates the two Lie algebras).
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_moment_translation {E : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {σ : LinearMap.BilinForm ℝ E} (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ)
    (γ : ℝ → AffineSymplecticGroup σ) (hγ : γ 0 = 1) (b' : E)
    (hC : HasDerivAt (fun t => (γ t).translation) b' 0) (Z : affineSymplecticAlgebra σ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t => moment σ (γ t).translation Z) (σ b' Z.1.2) 0

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.not_isCoboundary₁_moment_translation
declarations.doc:
The cohomology class of the affine symplectic group of a non-zero symplectic vector space is
NOT zero: `θ` is not a coboundary. On the translations `(id, C)` the coadjoint action fixes the
elements `(0, b)` of the Lie algebra, so every coboundary vanishes on them, whereas
`θ((id, C))(0, b) = -σ (b, C)`, which is non-zero for a suitable `b` by non-degeneracy. (By
Souriau's (11.21) this forbids a potential of `σ` invariant under the group; that implication is
not formalised here.)
declarations.statement:
lemma not_isCoboundary₁_moment_translation (hσ : IsSymplecticForm σ) (hE : ∃ v : E, v ≠ 0) :
    ¬ groupCohomology.IsCoboundary₁
      (fun a : AffineSymplecticGroup σ => moment σ a.translation)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.planeForm_not_isCoboundary₁
declarations.doc: The affine symplectic group of the symplectic plane has a non-zero cohomology class.
declarations.statement:
lemma planeForm_not_isCoboundary₁ :
    ¬ groupCohomology.IsCoboundary₁
      (fun a : AffineSymplecticGroup planeForm => moment planeForm a.translation)

modules.title: The mass as a cohomology class of the Galilean Lie algebra (Souriau)
modules.doc:
The total mass as a non-trivial cohomology class of the Galilean Lie algebra (Souriau).

## i. Overview

In chapter 12 of Structure des systèmes dynamiques (Dunod 1970), Souriau computes the moment of
the Galilean group acting on the evolution space of a system of material points. The moment is a
torsor `μ = {l, g, p, E}` (12.122)-(12.123): `l` is the angular momentum and `p` the momentum
(12.140), and `g = m R - p t` with `R` the centre of gravity (12.141). The Lagrange form `σ` of the
system satisfies (12.134), `σ(Z_V(y))(Z'_V(y)) = μ[Z, Z'] + m f₀(Z)(Z')`, where
`f₀(Z)(Z') = ⟨β, γ'⟩ - ⟨β', γ⟩` (12.130) and `m = Σ_j m_j` is the total mass (12.135). Souriau
remarks (12.136) that the total mass can be interpreted as characterising the corresponding
cohomology class of the Galilean group, and that this class is never zero.

This file proves these facts at the level of the Lie algebra for `N` free material points in
`ℝ³ = Fin 3 → ℝ` (no forces, `F_j = 0`; with the choice `B_j = 0` of (12.49), which (12.135)
imposes on an isolated system, (12.44) gives `E_j = 0` and (12.45) reduces to (12.40)). An element
`Z = (ω, β, γ, ε)` of the Galilean Lie algebra (12.74), (12.118) is a rotation `ω` (an axial
vector), a change of velocity `β`, a space translation `γ` and a time translation `ε`; it acts on
the evolution space, whose points are `y = (t, r_j, v_j)` (12.76), by the affine vector field
(12.119). The bracket is Souriau's (6.12 b), `[Z, Z']_V = [Z_V, Z'_V]`, where the bracket of two
vector fields is (2.45), here `DZ'_V(Z_V) - DZ_V(Z'_V)` (`EvolutionSpace.vectorField_bracket`);
this is the usual Lie bracket of vector fields (Mathlib's `VectorField.lieBracket`). The matrices
(12.74) are not formalised; on them this bracket reads `[Z, Z'] = Z'Z - ZZ'`, as in (11.22 a), the
opposite of the usual matrix commutator.

What is not formalised here:
- the Galilean group itself, its action (12.73), (12.76) and its cocycle `θ₀` (12.126)-(12.128),
  hence the statement of p. 151 that `θ₀` is not a coboundary of the group (definition (11.19)),
  used in (12.136). The algebra-level result of this file implies it, because the derivative of a
  group coboundary `Δ(μ₀)` is `μ₀[Z, Z']` (p. 116, note (1)); this implication is not formalised.
  Physlib has `GalileanGroup` in `Physlib.SpaceAndTime.GalileanGroup.Basic`, whose rotation part
  ranges over the full orthogonal group; Souriau's group (12.73) takes `A ∈ SO(3)` and is
  connected (p. 139). Both have the same Lie algebra, with which this file works in dimension `3`,
  in Souriau's parametrisation; the file links it to neither group;
- `GalileanAlgebra` has no vector space or `LieRing` structure here, only `Zero` and `Add`; the
  Jacobi identity is proved as an equation;
- that the vector field (12.119), taken as printed, is the derivative (6.11) of the action (12.76);
- the reading of (12.135) as the solution of the system (12.124), (12.134) for a general isolated
  system (`B_j = 0`, `Σ_j E_j = 0`, `Σ_j r_j × E_j = 0`): for free points the explicit moment and
  `m = Σ_j m_j` are verified, not derived; the uniqueness of `m` in (12.134) follows from
  `lagrangeForm_vectorField` and `smul_cocycle_isCoboundary_iff` but is not stated;
- the dimension `1` of (12.131), the second half of (12.136) (Hamilton's Lagrangian is not
  invariant), forces, the converse of (12.48), the invariance of `σ` (12.72), (12.76), and the
  uniqueness of the moment up to a constant (the constant in `E` is a choice);
- the evolution space is presymplectic, not symplectic (p. 148, (12.114));
  `EvolutionSpace.lagrangeForm_motion` shows that `σ` is degenerate, and `σ` depends on the point
  `y` through the velocities. The setting of `PhyslibAlpha.ClassicalMechanics.MomentMap.Basic`
  (a constant non-degenerate form on a vector space) therefore does not apply; the moment and the
  cocycle are computed explicitly.

## ii. Key results

- `GalileanAlgebra.bracket_jacobi`: the Jacobi identity for Souriau's bracket.
- `GalileanAlgebra.cocycle_cyclic`: (12.129), `f₀` satisfies the cyclic identity.
- `GalileanAlgebra.smul_cocycle_isCoboundary_iff`: `M f₀` is an algebra coboundary,
  `M f₀(Z)(Z') = μ₀[Z, Z']` for some torsor `μ₀`, if and only if `M = 0`.
- `EvolutionSpace.hasDerivAt_moment`: (12.124), the moment of the free points.
- `EvolutionSpace.moment_motion`: (12.121), the moment is constant along the free motions.
- `EvolutionSpace.lagrangeForm_vectorField`: (12.134) with `m = Σ_j m_j` (12.135).
- `EvolutionSpace.totalMass_cocycle_not_coboundary`: (12.136) at the level of the algebra, for a
  non-zero total mass the cocycle of the system is not a coboundary.
- `EvolutionSpace.moment_g`, `EvolutionSpace.centerOfMass_motion`: (12.141), `g = m R - p t`, and
  the uniform motion of the centre of gravity of free points.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Galilean Lie algebra
- B. Torsors
- C. The cocycle `f₀`
- D. The evolution space of free material points
- E. The moment
- F. The cocycle of the system and the mass

## iv. References

- J.-M. Souriau, Structure des systèmes dynamiques, Dunod, Paris, 1970: pp. 132-133
  (12.40)-(12.49), pp. 139-140 (12.72)-(12.76), p. 148 (12.114), pp. 150-153 (12.118)-(12.141);
  p. 27 (2.45), p. 50 (6.12 b) and p. 113 (11.22 a) for the bracket; p. 50 (6.13 b), p. 109
  (11.16), p. 114 (11.24) and p. 116, note (1), for the coboundaries of the algebra.

* J.-M. Souriau, *Structure des systèmes dynamiques*, Maîtrises de mathématiques, Dunod,
  Paris, 1970: chapter 12, pp. 132-153, and pp. 27, 50, 109, 113-116 for the conventions (2.45),
  (6.12), (6.13), (11.16), (11.22), (11.24). The equation numbers refer to this edition.
  [ref: Souriau1970]
