modules.title: A physical bielliptic counterexample
modules.doc:
Two actual Newtonian coasts realize a cheaper three-impulse maneuver.

## i. Overview

The first arc travels from radius 1 to the common apoapsis at 64. The second travels from that
apoapsis to radius 16. The three actual velocity jumps give the strict cost comparison.

## ii. Key results

- `BiellipticWitness.physical_three_impulse_counterexample` gives the main result of this module.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The two coasts and the three velocity jumps

## iv. References

- [ref: hohmann_weber_bielliptic]. Weber describes the three-burn bielliptic transfer geometry.

declarations.doc:
The numerical comparison is linked to actual finite-time coast arcs and
actual vector jump norms. No arrival time or third burn is sent to infinity.
declarations.statement:
lemma physical_three_impulse_counterexample :
    0 < totalTime ∧
    (∀ t, deriv (deriv (position first)) t =

modules.title: Lower bounds on the two Hohmann impulses
modules.doc:
Each impulse has a lower bound over the feasible invariant pairs.

## i. Overview

Split the comparison by signed angular momentum relative to the Hohmann value. Factoring the cost
difference gives a sum of nonnegative terms in each case.

## ii. Key results

- `first_square_lower_bound` gives the main result of this module.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The two squared cost inequalities

## iv. References

- [ref: hohmann_prussing_1992]. Prussing studies the two-impulse global comparison.

sections.text: ## A. The two squared cost inequalities

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.gap₁_low
declarations.doc: Exact nonnegative certificate on the h ≤ hH half-plane.
declarations.statement:
lemma gap₁_low (s : Shape) (w h : ℝ) :
    s.burnSquare₁ w h - s.burnH₁ ^ 2 =
      (w + 2*s.alpha - s.alpha^2*h^2) +
      (s.hH-h)*(2-s.alpha^2*(h+s.hH))

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.gap₁_high
declarations.statement:
lemma gap₁_high (s : Shape) (w h : ℝ) :
    s.burnSquare₁ w h - s.burnH₁ ^ 2 =
      (w+2-h^2) + (h-s.hH)*(h+s.hH-2)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.gap₂_low
declarations.statement:
lemma gap₂_low (s : Shape) (w h : ℝ) :
    s.burnSquare₂ w h - s.burnH₂ ^ 2 =
      (w+2*s.alpha-s.alpha^2*h^2) +
      s.alpha*(s.hH-h)*(2*s.circularOuter-s.alpha*(h+s.hH))

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.gap₂_high
declarations.statement:
lemma gap₂_high (s : Shape) (w h : ℝ) :
    s.burnSquare₂ w h - s.burnH₂ ^ 2 =
      (w+2-h^2) + (h-s.hH)*(h+s.hH-2*s.alpha*s.circularOuter)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.low_factor₁_pos
declarations.statement:
lemma low_factor₁_pos (s : Shape) {h : ℝ} (hh : h ≤ s.hH) :
    0 < 2 - s.alpha^2*(h+s.hH)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.low_factor₂_pos
declarations.statement:
lemma low_factor₂_pos (s : Shape) {h : ℝ} (hh : h ≤ s.hH) :
    0 < 2*s.circularOuter-s.alpha*(h+s.hH)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.high_factor₁_pos
declarations.statement:
lemma high_factor₁_pos (s : Shape) {h : ℝ} (hh : s.hH ≤ h) :
    0 < h+s.hH-2

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.high_factor₂_pos
declarations.statement:
lemma high_factor₂_pos (s : Shape) {h : ℝ} (hh : s.hH ≤ h) :
    0 < h+s.hH-2*s.alpha*s.circularOuter

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.first_square_lower_bound
declarations.doc: Every feasible competitor pays at least the Hohmann first impulse.
declarations.statement:
lemma first_square_lower_bound (s : Shape) {w h : ℝ} (hf : s.Feasible w h) :
    s.burnH₁ ^ 2 ≤ s.burnSquare₁ w h

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.second_square_lower_bound
declarations.doc: The second impulse separately also attains its global minimum at Hohmann.
declarations.statement:
lemma second_square_lower_bound (s : Shape) {w h : ℝ} (hf : s.Feasible w h) :
    s.burnH₂ ^ 2 ≤ s.burnSquare₂ w h

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.first_square_strict_of_h_ne
ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.invariant_pair_of_first_square_eq
declarations.doc:
The unique minimizer is an invariant pair, not a unique time-parametrized
trajectory: rotations and extra revolutions still have the same cost.

modules.title: Optimality over normalized endpoint velocities
modules.doc:
The Hohmann endpoint velocities minimize the total impulse.

## i. Overview

Conservation of normalized energy and signed angular momentum supplies the endpoint constraints.
Taking nonnegative square roots gives lower bounds for the two impulses and the equality
conditions.

## ii. Key results

- `endpoint_equality_characterization` gives the main result of this module.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The endpoint comparison and equality case

## iv. References

- [ref: hohmann_prussing_1992]. Prussing studies the two-impulse global comparison.

sections.text: ## A. The endpoint comparison and equality case

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.EndpointData
declarations.doc:
Two endpoint velocities in their own oriented radial/tangential frames.
The two conservation equalities are endpoint constraints, NOT a theorem that
arbitrary supplied data form a Kepler arc. Newton arcs are connected separately.
declarations.statement:
structure EndpointData (s : Shape) where
  /-- The normalized radial velocity at the inner endpoint. -/
  radial₁ : ℝ
  /-- The normalized prograde tangential velocity at the inner endpoint. -/
  tangent₁ : ℝ
  /-- The normalized radial velocity at the outer endpoint. -/
  radial₂ : ℝ
  /-- The normalized prograde tangential velocity at the outer endpoint. -/
  tangent₂ : ℝ
  /-- The endpoints have the same signed angular momentum. -/
  angular : tangent₂ = s.alpha * tangent₁
  /-- The endpoints have the same specific mechanical energy. -/
  energy : radial₁^2+tangent₁^2-2 = radial₂^2+tangent₂^2-2*s.alpha

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.EndpointData.w
declarations.doc: Twice the normalized specific energy of the endpoint data.
declarations.statement: def w {s : Shape} (z : EndpointData s) : ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.EndpointData.impulse₁
declarations.doc: The departure impulse magnitude for the normalized endpoint data.
declarations.statement: def impulse₁ {s : Shape} (z : EndpointData s) : ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.EndpointData.impulse₂
declarations.doc: The arrival impulse magnitude for the normalized endpoint data.
declarations.statement: def impulse₂ {s : Shape} (z : EndpointData s) : ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.EndpointData.cost
declarations.doc: The sum of the impulse magnitudes for the specified transfer.
declarations.statement: def cost {s : Shape} (z : EndpointData s) : ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.EndpointData.feasible
declarations.statement: lemma feasible {s : Shape} (z : EndpointData s) : s.Feasible z.w z.tangent₁

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.EndpointData.impulse₁_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma impulse₁_nonneg {s : Shape} (z : EndpointData s) : 0 ≤ z.impulse₁

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.EndpointData.impulse₂_nonneg
declarations.statement: lemma impulse₂_nonneg {s : Shape} (z : EndpointData s) : 0 ≤ z.impulse₂

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.EndpointData.impulse₁_sq
declarations.statement:
lemma impulse₁_sq {s : Shape} (z : EndpointData s) :
    z.impulse₁^2 = z.radial₁^2+(z.tangent₁-1)^2

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.EndpointData.impulse₂_sq
declarations.statement:
lemma impulse₂_sq {s : Shape} (z : EndpointData s) :
    z.impulse₂^2 = z.radial₂^2+(z.tangent₂-s.circularOuter)^2

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.EndpointData.impulse₁_sq_invariant
declarations.statement:
lemma impulse₁_sq_invariant {s : Shape} (z : EndpointData s) :
    z.impulse₁^2 = s.burnSquare₁ z.w z.tangent₁

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.EndpointData.impulse₂_sq_invariant
declarations.statement:
lemma impulse₂_sq_invariant {s : Shape} (z : EndpointData s) :
    z.impulse₂^2 = s.burnSquare₂ z.w z.tangent₁

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.endpoint_impulses_lower_bound
declarations.doc:
A global inequality over ALL feasible endpoint velocities, not merely a
stationary-point or small-perturbation calculation.
declarations.statement:
lemma endpoint_impulses_lower_bound (s : Shape) (z : EndpointData s) :
    s.burnH₁ ≤ z.impulse₁ ∧ s.burnH₂ ≤ z.impulse₂

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.endpoint_total_lower_bound
declarations.statement:
lemma endpoint_total_lower_bound (s : Shape) (z : EndpointData s) :
    s.costH ≤ z.cost

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.hohmannEndpoints
declarations.doc: A feasible corner achieving the lower bound; physical attainment is H1.
declarations.statement: def hohmannEndpoints (s : Shape) : EndpointData s

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.hohmannEndpoints_cost
declarations.statement: lemma hohmannEndpoints_cost (s : Shape) : (hohmannEndpoints s).cost = s.costH

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.endpoint_equality_characterization
declarations.doc:
Equality forces both endpoint radial velocities to vanish and fixes signed
angular momentum. No claim of uniqueness of flight time or orientation.
declarations.statement:
lemma endpoint_equality_characterization (s : Shape) (z : EndpointData s)
    (heq : z.cost = s.costH) :
    z.tangent₁ = s.hH ∧ z.tangent₂ = s.alpha*s.hH ∧
      z.radial₁ = 0 ∧ z.radial₂ = 0

modules.title: Hohmann optimality in the ideal rocket model
modules.doc:
Fixed positive exhaust speed transfers the impulse bound to propellant fraction.

## i. Overview

The ideal rocket equation gives the fraction consumed as a function of total delta-v at fixed
exhaust speed. Monotonicity transfers the two-impulse bound to this model.

## ii. Key results

- `newton_arc_ideal_fuel_lower_bound` gives the main result of this module.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The ideal propellant fraction

## iv. References

- [ref: hohmann_nasa_rocket]. NASA Glenn gives the ideal rocket equation.

sections.text: ## A. The ideal propellant fraction

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.idealPropellantFraction
declarations.doc: The fraction of initial mass consumed at fixed exhaust speed.
declarations.statement: def idealPropellantFraction (exhaustSpeed deltaV : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.idealPropellantFraction_mono
declarations.statement:
lemma idealPropellantFraction_mono {ve d₁ d₂ : ℝ} (hExhaustSpeed : 0 < ve) (hd : d₁ ≤ d₂) :
    idealPropellantFraction ve d₁ ≤ idealPropellantFraction ve d₂

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.idealPropellantFraction_strict
declarations.statement:
lemma idealPropellantFraction_strict {ve d₁ d₂ : ℝ} (hExhaustSpeed : 0 < ve) (hd : d₁ < d₂) :
    idealPropellantFraction ve d₁ < idealPropellantFraction ve d₂

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.remaining_fraction_two_burns
declarations.doc:
Equal exhaust speed makes multiplying burn mass ratios equivalent to using
sum delta-v; this is the ONLY fuel interpretation used here.
declarations.statement:
lemma remaining_fraction_two_burns (ve d₁ d₂ : ℝ) :
    Real.exp (-d₁/ve)*Real.exp (-d₂/ve) = Real.exp (-(d₁+d₂)/ve)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.newton_arc_ideal_fuel_lower_bound
declarations.statement:
lemma newton_arc_ideal_fuel_lower_bound (p : Units) (a : KeplerArc p.mu)
    (h₀ : (a.state a.t₀).radius=p.r₁) (h₁ : (a.state a.t₁).radius=p.r₂)
    {ve : ℝ} (hExhaustSpeed : 0 < ve) :
    idealPropellantFraction ve p.bound ≤ idealPropellantFraction ve
      ((a.state a.t₀).impulse p.speed+(a.state a.t₁).impulse p.circular₂)

modules.title: Attainment of the Hohmann lower bound
modules.doc:
The explicit Hohmann trajectory attains the lower bound within the comparison class.

## i. Overview

The apsidal speeds in the explicit transfer match the normalized optimal speeds. Taking real and
imaginary parts of the Newtonian coast gives a member of the very same comparison class used for
the lower bound.

## ii. Key results

- `h1_global_two_impulse_minimum` gives the main result of this module.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Physical attainment and the minimum

## iv. References

- [ref: hohmann_prussing_1992]. Prussing studies the two-impulse global comparison.

sections.text: ## A. Physical attainment and the minimum

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.unitsOfH1
declarations.doc: Data conversion only; no optimality assumption is added to H1.
declarations.statement: def unitsOfH1 (p : HohmannTransfer.Parameters) : Units

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.h1_speed
declarations.statement:
lemma h1_speed (p : HohmannTransfer.Parameters) :
    (unitsOfH1 p).speed=HohmannTransfer.circularSpeed p.mu p.r₁

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.h1_outer_speed
declarations.statement:
lemma h1_outer_speed (p : HohmannTransfer.Parameters) :
    (unitsOfH1 p).circular₂=HohmannTransfer.circularSpeed p.mu p.r₂

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.h1_peri_speed
declarations.statement:
lemma h1_peri_speed (p : HohmannTransfer.Parameters) :
    (unitsOfH1 p).speed*(unitsOfH1 p).shape.hH=HohmannTransfer.periSpeed p

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.h1_apo_speed
declarations.statement:
lemma h1_apo_speed (p : HohmannTransfer.Parameters) :
    (unitsOfH1 p).speed*((unitsOfH1 p).shape.alpha*(unitsOfH1 p).shape.hH)=
      HohmannTransfer.apoSpeed p

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.h1_bound_eq_totalDeltaV
declarations.statement:
lemma h1_bound_eq_totalDeltaV (p : HohmannTransfer.Parameters) :
    (unitsOfH1 p).bound=HohmannTransfer.totalDeltaV p

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.h1_global_two_impulse_minimum
declarations.doc:
Physical attainment from H1 plus a global lower bound against arbitrary
smooth two-impulse competitors. Free time, free phase, fixed central field.
declarations.statement:
lemma h1_global_two_impulse_minimum (p : HohmannTransfer.Parameters) :
    (∀ t, deriv (deriv (HohmannTransfer.position p)) t =
      -(p.mu/‖HohmannTransfer.position p t‖^3) • HohmannTransfer.position p t) ∧
    HohmannTransfer.position p 0=HohmannTransfer.pack p.r₁ 0 ∧
    HohmannTransfer.position p p.transferTime=HohmannTransfer.pack (-p.r₂) 0 ∧
    (unitsOfH1 p).bound=
      ‖HohmannTransfer.entryImpulse p‖+‖HohmannTransfer.exitImpulse p‖ ∧
    (∀ a : KeplerArc p.mu,
      (a.state a.t₀).radius=p.r₁ → (a.state a.t₁).radius=p.r₂ →
      HohmannTransfer.totalDeltaV p ≤
        (a.state a.t₀).impulse (HohmannTransfer.circularSpeed p.mu p.r₁)+
        (a.state a.t₁).impulse (HohmannTransfer.circularSpeed p.mu p.r₂))

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.h1KeplerArc
declarations.doc: The explicit H1 coast is a member of the same class used for the lower bound.
declarations.statement: def h1KeplerArc (p : HohmannTransfer.Parameters) : KeplerArc p.mu

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.h1_state_radius
declarations.statement:
lemma h1_state_radius (p : HohmannTransfer.Parameters) (t : ℝ) :
    ((h1KeplerArc p).state t).radius = ‖HohmannTransfer.position p t‖

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.h1_attains_bound_in_kepler_class
declarations.doc: The lower bound is attained within the actual Newtonian comparison class.
declarations.statement:
lemma h1_attains_bound_in_kepler_class (p : HohmannTransfer.Parameters) :
    ∃ a : KeplerArc p.mu,
      (a.state a.t₀).radius = p.r₁ ∧ (a.state a.t₁).radius = p.r₂ ∧
      (a.state a.t₀).impulse (unitsOfH1 p).speed +
        (a.state a.t₁).impulse (unitsOfH1 p).circular₂ = (unitsOfH1 p).bound

modules.title: Kepler conservation and two-impulse bounds
modules.doc:
Newtonian coast arcs supply the endpoint invariants needed for the cost bound.

## i. Overview

A comparison arc has differentiable position and velocity and avoids the centre throughout a
finite interval. The Newtonian equation gives constant energy and angular momentum without
restricting their signs.

## ii. Key results

- `KeplerArc.newton_arc_lower_bound` gives the main result of this module.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Conservation along an arbitrary comparison arc

## iv. References

- [ref: hohmann_prussing_1992]. Prussing studies the two-impulse global comparison.

sections.text: ## A. Conservation along an arbitrary comparison arc

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.KeplerArc
declarations.doc: A noncollision Newtonian coast over a positive finite time interval.
declarations.statement:
structure KeplerArc (mu : ℝ) where
  /-- The time of the departure impulse. -/
  t₀ : ℝ
  /-- The time of the arrival impulse. -/
  t₁ : ℝ
  /-- The coast takes positive time. -/
  time_order : t₀ < t₁
  /-- The first Cartesian position coordinate as a function of time. -/
  x : ℝ → ℝ
  /-- The second Cartesian position coordinate as a function of time. -/
  y : ℝ → ℝ
  /-- The first Cartesian velocity coordinate as a function of time. -/
  vx : ℝ → ℝ
  /-- The second Cartesian velocity coordinate as a function of time. -/
  vy : ℝ → ℝ
  /-- The coast stays away from the attracting centre. -/
  radius_pos : ∀ t ∈ Icc t₀ t₁, 0 < Real.sqrt (x t^2+y t^2)
  /-- The first position derivative is the first velocity component. -/
  dx : ∀ t ∈ Icc t₀ t₁, HasDerivAt x (vx t) t
  /-- The second position derivative is the second velocity component. -/
  dy : ∀ t ∈ Icc t₀ t₁, HasDerivAt y (vy t) t
  /-- The first velocity derivative obeys Newtonian central acceleration. -/
  dvx : ∀ t ∈ Icc t₀ t₁,
    HasDerivAt vx (-mu*x t/(Real.sqrt (x t^2+y t^2))^3) t
  /-- The second velocity derivative obeys Newtonian central acceleration. -/
  dvy : ∀ t ∈ Icc t₀ t₁,
    HasDerivAt vy (-mu*y t/(Real.sqrt (x t^2+y t^2))^3) t

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.KeplerArc.state
declarations.doc: The Cartesian state of the coast at the given time.
declarations.statement: def state {mu : ℝ} (a : KeplerArc mu) (t : ℝ) : PlanarState

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.KeplerArc.left_mem
declarations.statement: lemma left_mem {mu : ℝ} (a : KeplerArc mu) : a.t₀ ∈ Icc a.t₀ a.t₁

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.KeplerArc.right_mem
declarations.statement: lemma right_mem {mu : ℝ} (a : KeplerArc mu) : a.t₁ ∈ Icc a.t₀ a.t₁

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.KeplerArc.radius_deriv
declarations.statement:
lemma radius_deriv {mu t : ℝ} (a : KeplerArc mu) (ht : t ∈ Icc a.t₀ a.t₁) :
    HasDerivAt (fun u => (a.state u).radius)
      ((a.x t*a.vx t+a.y t*a.vy t)/(a.state t).radius) t

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.KeplerArc.angular_deriv_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma angular_deriv_zero {mu t : ℝ} (a : KeplerArc mu) (ht : t ∈ Icc a.t₀ a.t₁) :
    HasDerivAt (fun u => (a.state u).angular) 0 t

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.KeplerArc.energy_deriv_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma energy_deriv_zero {mu t : ℝ} (a : KeplerArc mu) (ht : t ∈ Icc a.t₀ a.t₁) :
    HasDerivAt (fun u => (a.state u).energy mu) 0 t

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.KeplerArc.equal_endpoints_of_zero_deriv
declarations.statement:
lemma equal_endpoints_of_zero_deriv {f : ℝ → ℝ} {a b : ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b)
    (hd : ∀ t ∈ Icc a b, HasDerivAt f 0 t) : f b=f a

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.KeplerArc.energy_conserved
declarations.statement:
lemma energy_conserved {mu : ℝ} (a : KeplerArc mu) :
    (a.state a.t₀).energy mu = (a.state a.t₁).energy mu

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.KeplerArc.angular_conserved
declarations.statement:
lemma angular_conserved {mu : ℝ} (a : KeplerArc mu) :
    (a.state a.t₀).angular = (a.state a.t₁).angular

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.KeplerArc.endpoints
declarations.doc:
Obtain endpoint constraints from the actual ODE; no conservation law is an
input field of KeplerArc. Endpoint orientation and coast time are unrestricted.

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.KeplerArc.newton_arc_lower_bound
declarations.doc:
Global two-impulse lower bound for every noncollision Newtonian coast arc.
No tangency, ellipse, energy sign or positive angular momentum is assumed.
declarations.statement:
lemma newton_arc_lower_bound (p : Units) (a : KeplerArc p.mu)
    (h₀ : (a.state a.t₀).radius=p.r₁) (h₁ : (a.state a.t₁).radius=p.r₂) :
    p.bound ≤ (a.state a.t₀).impulse p.speed + (a.state a.t₁).impulse p.circular₂

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.KeplerArc.newton_arc_equality_endpoints
declarations.doc: Equality of the actual Cartesian cost forces the Hohmann endpoint velocities.
declarations.statement:
lemma newton_arc_equality_endpoints (p : Units) (a : KeplerArc p.mu)
    (h₀ : (a.state a.t₀).radius = p.r₁) (h₁ : (a.state a.t₁).radius = p.r₂)
    (he : (a.state a.t₀).impulse p.speed + (a.state a.t₁).impulse p.circular₂ = p.bound) :
    (a.state a.t₀).radial = 0 ∧ (a.state a.t₁).radial = 0 ∧
    (a.state a.t₀).tangent = p.speed * p.shape.hH ∧
    (a.state a.t₁).tangent = p.speed * (p.shape.alpha * p.shape.hH)

modules.title: Restoring physical units to the Hohmann bounds
modules.doc:
The normalized lower bound scales by the inner circular speed.

## i. Overview

The physical radial and tangential endpoint components are normalized by the inner circular
speed. The cost scales linearly and the feasibility equations are preserved.

## ii. Key results

- `PhysicalEndpoints.physical_lower_bound` gives the main result of this module.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Physical endpoint data and normalization

## iv. References

- [ref: hohmann_prussing_1992]. Prussing studies the two-impulse global comparison.

sections.text: ## A. Physical endpoint data and normalization

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.Units
declarations.doc: The gravitational parameter and the ordered physical radii for the comparison.
declarations.statement:
structure Units where
  /-- The central gravitational parameter. -/
  mu : ℝ
  /-- The radius of the inner circular orbit. -/
  r₁ : ℝ
  /-- The radius of the outer circular orbit. -/
  r₂ : ℝ
  /-- The gravitational parameter is positive. -/
  mu_pos : 0 < mu
  /-- The inner radius is positive. -/
  r₁_pos : 0 < r₁
  /-- The outer radius exceeds the inner radius. -/
  outward : r₁ < r₂

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.Units.r₂_pos
declarations.statement: lemma r₂_pos (p : Units) : 0 < p.r₂

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.Units.r₁_ne
declarations.statement: lemma r₁_ne (p : Units) : p.r₁ ≠ 0

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.Units.r₂_ne
declarations.statement: lemma r₂_ne (p : Units) : p.r₂ ≠ 0

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.Units.shape
declarations.doc: The reciprocal radius ratio associated with the physical radii.
declarations.statement: def shape (p : Units) : Shape

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.Units.speed
declarations.doc: The inner circular speed used as the unit of velocity.

modules.title: Planar states for the Hohmann comparison
modules.doc:
Cartesian velocity jumps can be evaluated in polar components.

## i. Overview

The endpoint velocity is compared with the prograde circular velocity at the same position. The
squared Euclidean norm decomposes into a radial square and a tangential difference squared.

## ii. Key results

- `PlanarState.impulse_polar` gives the main result of this module.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Cartesian and polar endpoint data

## iv. References

- [ref: hohmann_prussing_1992]. Prussing studies the two-impulse global comparison.

modules.title: Global two-impulse Hohmann bounds
modules.doc:
Every allowed Newtonian comparison arc satisfies the Hohmann lower bound.

## i. Overview

The global comparison is over two impulses between coplanar circular orbits with the same
orientation. The coast has free time and phase. A finite three-impulse cost comparison
distinguishes the larger class.

## ii. Key results

- `global_two_impulse_newton_lower_bound` gives the main result of this module.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The lower bound and the finite cost comparison

## iv. References

- [ref: hohmann_prussing_1992]. Prussing studies the two-impulse global comparison.

sections.text: ## A. The lower bound and the finite cost comparison

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.global_two_impulse_endpoint_optimality
declarations.doc:
Global means all feasible TWO-impulse, coplanar, co-oriented circle-to-circle
transfers, with free departure phase and flight time. A coast may have radial
velocity, negative momentum, or nonnegative energy. No third burn is allowed.
declarations.statement:
lemma global_two_impulse_endpoint_optimality (s : Shape) :
    (∀ z : EndpointData s, s.costH ≤ z.cost) ∧
    (hohmannEndpoints s).cost=s.costH ∧
    (∀ z : EndpointData s, z.cost=s.costH →
      z.tangent₁=s.hH ∧ z.tangent₂=s.alpha*s.hH ∧
      z.radial₁=0 ∧ z.radial₂=0)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.global_two_impulse_newton_lower_bound
declarations.doc:
The global inequality applies to genuinely differentiable Newtonian coast
arcs; conservation is proved in KeplerConservation rather than postulated.
declarations.statement:
lemma global_two_impulse_newton_lower_bound (p : Units) (a : KeplerArc p.mu)
    (h₀ : (a.state a.t₀).radius=p.r₁) (h₁ : (a.state a.t₁).radius=p.r₂) :
    p.bound ≤ (a.state a.t₀).impulse p.speed+(a.state a.t₁).impulse p.circular₂

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.HohmannOptimality.finite_three_impulse_counterexample
declarations.doc:
An unrestricted all-maneuver assertion is false: a finite 1→64→16
bielliptic construction has strictly smaller delta-v than Hohmann 1→16.
declarations.statement:
lemma finite_three_impulse_counterexample :
    (9/1000 : ℝ) < Bielliptic.hohmannCost 16 - Bielliptic.cost Bielliptic.«example»

modules.title: Dimensionless Hohmann parameters
modules.doc:
The reciprocal radius ratio determines the normalized Hohmann cost.

## i. Overview

Use the inner radius and its circular speed as units. The Hohmann invariant pair lies at the
intersection of two inequalities for the squared radial speeds.

## ii. Key results

- `Shape.corner_feasible` gives the main result of this module.

## iii. Table of contents

## iv. References

- [ref: hohmann_prussing_1992]. Prussing studies the two-impulse global comparison.

modules.title: Lagrange's circular equilateral solution
modules.doc:
Three positive masses form a rotating equilateral triangle in a Newtonian gravitational system.

## i. Overview

A triangle of side length `ℓ` is translated to its mass barycentre. Rotating it with angular
speed `√(G * M / ℓ ^ 3)`, where `M` is the total mass, preserves the separation of each pair.
The gravitational acceleration of each particle is therefore the centripetal acceleration
of its rotation. The rotating trajectories define particles in an arbitrary planar inertial
reference frame, and `NewtonianSystem.ofGravity` supplies the system and both Newton laws.

## ii. Key results

- `exists_lagrange_equilateral_solution` gives the three labelled particles, their equilateral
  distances, uniform circular motion about the barycentre, and Kepler's third law.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The rotating configuration
- B. Particles in the inertial frame
- C. The Lagrange solution

## iv. References

* [ref: chenciner_fejoz_2008], §8, for the reduction of the equilateral force sum.
* R5 Lean formalization.
  https://github.com/hkjtsgmc79-boop/lagrange-three-body-lean/releases/tag/v0.5.1

sections.text: ## A. The rotating configuration
## B. Particles in the inertial frame
## C. The Lagrange solution

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.LagrangeOrbit.exists_lagrange_equilateral_solution
declarations.doc:
The Lagrange relative equilibrium for three positive masses in a planar inertial frame.
The labelled particles move on a rigid equilateral triangle about their mass barycentre,
with a positive common period obeying Kepler's third law.
declarations.statement:
public lemma exists_lagrange_equilateral_solution (frame : ReferenceFrame 2) [Fact frame.IsInertial]
    (hG : 0 < G) (hℓ : 0 < ℓ) :
    ∃ (system : NewtonianSystem 2) (e : Fin 3 ≃ system.Particle) (T : ℝ),
      system.frame = frame ∧
      system.internalForces = gravityForces G system.particles ∧
      system.externalForces = 0 ∧
      (∀ i, (e i).mass = m i) ∧
      (∀ t, ∑ i, (m i).val • (e i).pos t = 0) ∧
      (∀ t i j, i ≠ j → ‖(e i).pos t - (e j).pos t‖ = ℓ) ∧
      (∀ i, Function.Periodic (e i).pos T) ∧
      (∃ plane : ℂ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] system.frame.Vector, ∀ t i,
        (e i).pos t = plane (rotation (Circle.exp (2 * Real.pi / T * t))
          (plane.symm ((e i).pos 0)))) ∧
      0 < T ∧ T ^ 2 * (G * ∑ i, (m i).val) = 4 * Real.pi ^ 2 * ℓ ^ 3

modules.title: Pairwise Newtonian gravitation
modules.doc:
Pair forces for a finite collection of point particles in a reference frame.

## i. Overview

For a source of mass `m`, the gravitational acceleration of a target is proportional to
`G * m` times the displacement towards the source divided by the cube of the separation.
Here `G` is the gravitational constant in the frame's units. The force multiplies the
acceleration by the target mass. Each ordered pair of distinct particle occurrences supplies
one internal force, preserving multiplicities in the particle multiset.

The formulas use the frame's physical norm. They model Newtonian gravity at collision-free
times. At coincidence the Lean expression has value zero by totalized division.

## ii. Key results

- `ReferenceFrame.gravityForces_reverse` proves Newton's third law for the force multiset.
- `ReferenceFrame.netForce_gravity` expresses the net force as mass times acceleration.
- `PointParticle.NewtonianSystem.ofGravity` bundles a solution of the acceleration equations
  as a Newtonian system in an inertial frame.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Gravitational forces and acceleration
- B. Newtonian systems under gravity

## iv. References

* [ref: goldstein_classicalmechanics], Chapter 3, for the inverse-square gravitational force.

sections.text: ## A. Gravitational forces and acceleration
## B. Newtonian systems under gravity

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.pairGravityAcceleration
declarations.doc: The contribution of the source to the target's gravitational acceleration.
declarations.statement: def pairGravityAcceleration (source target : particles) (t : ℝ) : frame.Vector

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.gravityAcceleration
declarations.doc: The target's gravitational acceleration from all other particle occurrences.
declarations.statement: def gravityAcceleration (target : particles) (t : ℝ) : frame.Vector

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.pairGravity
declarations.doc: The Newtonian force exerted by one particle on another in the given frame.
declarations.statement:
def pairGravity (source target : particles) (hne : source ≠ target) :
    frame.InternalForce particles

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.pairGravity_reverse
declarations.doc: Exchanging source and target gives the equal and opposite force.
declarations.statement:
lemma pairGravity_reverse (source target : particles) (hne : source ≠ target) :
    (pairGravity G particles source target hne).reverse =
      pairGravity G particles target source hne.symm

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.GravityPairs
declarations.doc: All ordered pairs of distinct particle occurrences, grouped by target.
declarations.statement: abbrev GravityPairs

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.gravityForces
declarations.doc: The internal gravitational forces, with each ordered pair occurring once.
declarations.statement: def gravityForces : Multiset (frame.InternalForce particles)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.gravityForces_reverse
declarations.doc: Newton's third law for the collection of pairwise gravitational forces.
declarations.statement:
lemma gravityForces_reverse :
    (gravityForces G particles).map InternalForce.reverse = gravityForces G particles

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.netForce_gravity
declarations.doc: The net internal force is the target mass times its gravitational acceleration.
declarations.statement:
lemma netForce_gravity (target : particles) (t : ℝ) :
    netForce target (gravityForces G particles) 0 t =
      target.1.mass • gravityAcceleration G particles target t

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.acceleration_eq_gravity_iff
declarations.doc:
In an inertial frame, the gravitational acceleration equation is equivalent to Newton's
second law for the constructed internal forces.
declarations.statement:
lemma acceleration_eq_gravity_iff [Fact frame.IsInertial]
    (target : particles) (t : ℝ) :
    target.1.acceleration t = gravityAcceleration G particles target t ↔
      netForce target (gravityForces G particles) 0 t =
        target.1.mass • target.1.acceleration t

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.PointParticle.NewtonianSystem.ofGravity
declarations.doc:
Bundle particles that follow the gravitational equations of motion as a Newtonian system
with no external forces. The inverse-square law describes the motion at collision-free times.
declarations.statement:
def ofGravity (G : ℝ) (particles : Multiset frame.Particle)
    (motion : ∀ (target : particles) (t : ℝ),
      target.1.acceleration t = gravityAcceleration G particles target t) :
    NewtonianSystem d
